papers.title: Finiteness of planar central configurations of six bodies for all positive masses: Part I, exceptional-mass first limits
papers.abstract: We separate the generic positive-mass finiteness problem for planar six-body central configurations from finiteness on exceptional mass loci. The Chang--Chen diagram enumeration has 117 graphs. The arguments below confine 40 first-limit diagram obligations to proper necessary mass loci. In particular, a direct function-field argument establishes the No.~66 mass condition for both zero and nonzero drift. We establish the algebraic reduction from an infinite positive family to a germ with an unbounded seven-product, and use the stated diagram rules and computational certificates to confine its mass vector to the union of these loci. Finiteness on the exceptional positive mass loci, the proposed subject of Part II, will be discussed in another paper.

papers.title: Inferring the delay time distribution of type Ia supernovae with CAALAM I: SED modelling choices and their effect on the delay time distribution
papers.abstract: A delay time distribution (DTD) quantifies the lag between progenitor formation and the subsequent explosive event. The DTD for a sample of Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) from a survey can be modelled through relative rates and the star formation histories (SFH) of all individual galaxies. Modern wide-field surveys require computationally efficient methods to model the DTD without modelling large samples of non-host galaxies. We model the DTD for a volume limited sample from SNe Ia from the Zwicky Transient Facility. The aim is to study the effect of varying SED modelling assumptions, including stellar templates, dust attenuation, SFH models, and photometric coverage. We present a new modelling framework, the Conditional Astral Ancestry Latency Analysis Machine (CAALAM), to infer the DTD of a sample of SNe Ia from the posterior of their host galaxy SFH. A model consisting of a standard stellar template, a non-parametric SFH and a flexible dust attenuation law, is favoured by the data and predicts a non-parametric DTD peaking at 100-330 Myr. When modelled as a power law, the DTD has a characteristic exponent of $-1.30 \pm 0.04$. The exponent is sensitive to dust attenuation, photometry, or SFH. When the DTD is convolved with the SFHs of the host galaxies, we find a bimodal progenitor age distribution, with $\sim60\%$ of progenitors with ages around 1.1-3.6 Gyr and the remaining progenitors older than 3.6 Gyr. We show a correspondence between the modes of the distributions of SN Ia light curve stretch and the progenitor ages. Our inferred DTD implies that most SNe Ia ($\sim 60\%$) occur promptly within 330 Myr of progenitor formation. However, the implied progenitor ages from the DTD convolved with the SFHs from our sample are significantly older. This suggests that the DTD might be a mixture of a prompt and an extended progenitor channel.

authors.name: Jens Hjorth
authors.institution: Laboratoire d’Etudes du Rayonnement et de la Matière en Astrophysique et Atmosphères

papers.title: Stability and Nonlinear Dynamics of Field-Driven Extended Domain Walls with Interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya Interaction
papers.abstract: We analyze the stability and non-linear dynamics of extended domain walls (DWs) with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI) driven by an external magnetic field in the clean limit (i.e., in the absence of disorder and thermal fluctuations). We show that for moderate DMI strengths, the dynamics in both the low- and high-field regimes are accurately described by a rigid-wall Walker model that neglects flexural degrees of freedom. At intermediate fields, however, the system undergoes a transition into a non-trivial spatio-temporally chaotic regime characterized by dynamically roughened domain walls displaying single- or multi-valued profiles. The phase boundaries delimiting this regime in the magnetic field-DMI phase space are computed using a linear stability analysis based on Floquet theory applied to the extended domain wall, explicitly accounting for DMI and internal phase dynamics. Our theoretical analysis and predicted phase diagram are fully supported by numerical micromagnetic simulations solving the full Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation.

authors.name: Alberto Rosso
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

authors.name: Alejandro B. Kolton
authors.institution: Consejo Nacional de Investigaciones Científicas y Técnicas

papers.title: Charmenability of twin building lattices
papers.abstract: Let $Λ= \mathcal G_A (\mathbb F_q)$ be a minimal simply connected split Kac-Moody group of compact-hyperbolic type, and set $Γ=Λ/Z(Λ)$. We prove that $Γ$ is charfinite when $q\geq 11$, or when its Weyl group is $3$-spherical and $q\geq 4$. Here are a few consequences: the only characters of $Γ$ are the trivial and regular characters, every invariant random subgroup is supported on $\{e\}$ and $Γ$ and these are the only uniformly recurrent subgroups, and every nontrivial unitary $Γ$-representation weakly contains the regular representation. Our approach relies on a recent result due to Caprace and Thom, showing that the topological completions $G_+$ and $G_-$ associated to $Γ$ have the Howe-Moore property. We prove a criterion of charmenability for irreducible lattices with trivial amenable radical in products of Howe-Moore groups acting geometrically on proper hyperbolic spaces. The criterion requires the visual boundaries to be Poisson boundaries of suitable random walks and the corresponding lattice actions to be essentially free.

papers.title: Hydrodynamics and propulsive efficiency of stern-sculling propulsion
papers.abstract: Stern-sculling is a traditional form of human-powered boat propulsion in which a single oar is oscillated laterally at the stern. In this study, we investigate this propulsion technique from a hydrodynamic perspective by continuously measuring the oar kinematics, the boat motion, and the forces acting on the oar across a broad range of boat speeds. During the lateral strokes, lift serves as the main propulsive force, whereas during the backward strokes, propulsion is primarily associated with added-mass effects. These measurements allow us to determine the propulsive efficiency as a function of boat speed. The efficiency peaks at approximately 65\% at an intermediate speed and then decreases progressively to approximately 25\% at higher speeds. These results provide insight into the hydrodynamic mechanisms governing this traditional mode of propulsion and highlight the effectiveness of stern-sculling at moderate speeds.

authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

authors.name: Marc Rabaud

papers.title: Predictable Scaling: Efficient Model Exploration via Scaling-Law Prediction
papers.abstract: Evaluating candidate changes (hypotheses) to recommendation models requires full-scale training runs consuming thousands of GPU-hours, severely limiting the hypothesis space engineers can feasibly explore. We introduce Predictable Scaling (PS), a systematic framework that exploits empirically verified regularity conditions to predict full-scale model performance from small-scale proxies. PS constructs scaled-down variants via composable scaling functions along distinct resource axes, and projects metrics to the target scale via curve fitting with calibrated uncertainty estimates. We compare three prediction strategies of increasing expressiveness: even the simplest (raw proxy) achieves prediction error within the empirical noise floor of repeated-run variance; the most expressive (Gaussian Process) provides an indicative 15% relative MAE improvement and calibrated uncertainty. Evaluation on two ranking models of increasing complexity---a task-specific model and a foundation model---demonstrates that PS correctly ranks actionable hypotheses across diverse hypothesis types at 79-88% compute reductions.

papers.title: Towards optimal selection schedules for online active learning
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of online linear classification, where a stream of unlabeled samples is available, and annotation is costly. We investigate the optimal query policy, that prescribes whether and when a sample should be labeled and used for a training step, or instead discarded, so as to minimize a given objective. We focus on the realizable case, under Gaussian design, in the high-dimensional regime where data dimension and number of unlabeled samples grow proportionally. We consider two objectives: 1) the generalization error under a labeling budget, and 2) a cumulative cost function where mistakes have unit cost and queries cost $Δ$. We first show that the myopic policies that greedily minimize at all times the increment in the objective correspond to either small or intermediate-margin policies, that prescribe the selection of samples whose margins fall within certain intervals that shrink with time. Within this class, we numerically ascertain the optimal schedules for the selection thresholds that minimize the final values of the objectives. Taking inspiration from the myopic policy for the cumulative cost, we design a very simple query policy schedule that we compare to other proposed heuristics, on synthetic data and real medical image datasets. Finally, we discuss myopic policies for two-layer neural networks, and exemplify how naive margin-based policies can cease to be optimal.

authors.name: Hugo Cui
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Primal-dual forward-reflected splitting with linesearch for distributed min-max problems under local Lipschitz smoothness
papers.abstract: We consider a network of finitely many agents aiming to cooperatively solve a convex-concave min-max problem combining nonsmooth terms with a smooth saddle function whose partial gradients are only locally Lipschitz continuous. Without requiring prior knowledge of the local Lipschitz moduli of the partial gradients, we propose a distributed proximal-reflected-gradient algorithm which incorporates a distributed backtracking procedure to adjust the stepsizes at each iteration. The algorithm is derived by reformulating the min-max problem as a composite monotone inclusion involving the sum of a maximally monotone operator, a linearly composed maximally monotone operator, and a single-valued locally Lipschitz continuous monotone operator. To solve this inclusion, we introduce a novel primal-dual forward-reflected splitting method with linesearch and establish its convergence using a Lyapunov-based analysis. In addition, when specialised to the min-max formulation, we derive an $\mathcal{O}(1/N)$ ergodic convergence rate for a consensus-penalised gap function. Finally, applying this splitting framework with mixing matrices yields our distributed method for consensus min-max optimisation.

authors.name: Felipe Atenas
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: On conservativity of multitype continuous-state branching processes
papers.abstract: In [4], Grey gives a condition on the branching mechanism $ψ$ of a continuous- state branching process Z ensuring that the process is conservative. This condition is obtained from the expression of the solution of the differential equation satisfied by the Laplace exponent of Z. In higher dimensions, it is generally no longer possible to make this solution explicit and very few conditions ensuring the conservativity of the process are known. In this paper, we provide necessary conditions and sufficient conditions for conservativity. For dimension 2, when types cannot regenerate themselves, we give a necessary and sufficient condition and we invert the Lamperti representation of the multitype branching process.

authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

authors.name: Clément Lamoureux
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: On the Power of Alternating Local Certification with Constant-Size Certificates
papers.abstract: We study alternation hierarchies for distributed decision in anonymous networks with constant-size certificates. A prover and a disprover alternately assign certificates to nodes over a constant number of rounds, after which each node decides whether to accept based on its own input and the certificates observed in its neighborhood. An instance is accepted if all nodes accept. Unlike previous work on distributed alternation hierarchies, which considered restricted local computation (Reiter, PODC 2024) or logarithmic-size certificates (Feuilloley et al., ICALP 2016), we focus on constant-size certificates and the role of neighborhood information in determining expressive power. We consider three models: SET, where nodes observe only the set of certificate sequences of their neighbors; MULTISET, where multiplicities are also visible; and PORTS, where neighbors can additionally be distinguished by local port numbers. We establish that SET is strictly weaker than MULTISET, which is in turn strictly weaker than PORTS, and that all three alternation hierarchies are strict at every level. Despite their severe restrictions, these models are remarkably expressive: LEADER belongs to the third level of SET. Our main characterization shows that, over finite input alphabets, SET coincides exactly with monadic second-order logic (MSO$_1$). Moreover, every language definable in counting monadic second-order logic (CMSO$_1$) belongs to PORTS, while MULTISET already contains languages that are not CMSO$_1$-definable. Nevertheless, this expressive power has fundamental limitations. PORTS does not capture MSO$_2$: neither Hamiltonicity nor the existence of a perfect matching belongs to PORTS. Furthermore, over unbounded input alphabets, PORTS cannot verify that every node has been given the correct network size.

authors.name: Guillaume Theyssier
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Symmetry constraints on magnon-induced dynamics of skyrmion helicity in frustrated magnets
papers.abstract: The helicity of a magnetic skyrmion in a centrosymmetric frustrated magnet is a soft collective coordinate and a candidate variable for encoding quantum information. Its coherence is ultimately influenced by coupling to the magnon environment, which is commonly incorporated only phenomenologically. Here we combine a microscopic Keldysh treatment of the helicity--magnon coupling to resolve the contribution of individual magnon modes to the effective helicity dynamics. In the U(1)-symmetric model, the magnon bath generates, to leading order, a reactive helicity mass renormalization. When U(1) symmetry is broken, additional direct helicity--magnon couplings become allowed. In the presence of finite magnon lifetimes, these couplings generate an Ohmic contribution to the low-frequency helicity dynamics. The spatial symmetry of the perturbation determines which magnon sectors contribute to this damping, providing mode-resolved selection rules for the helicity--magnon coupling. Thus, we establish a microscopic connection between helicity dynamics and the excitation spectrum of frustrated skyrmions and identify the symmetry constraints governing dissipation of helicity-based quantum states.

authors.name: Christina Psaroudaki
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: The maximum number of Hamiltonian cycles in tournaments
papers.abstract: Let $C(n)$ denote the maximum number of directed Hamiltonian cycles in a tournament on $n$ vertices. We prove that, as $n\to\infty$, $$ C(n) = \left(\frac{\cosh 1}{\cos 1}\pm o(1)\right)\frac{(n-1)!}{2^n}. $$ The bound is asymptotically attained by the regular tournament with vertices $\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z$ where $(i,j)$ is a directed edge if $j - i \pmod n< n/2$. This answers a question of Alon and proves a conjecture of Wormald. Among the other implications of these results is asymptotically determining the maximum number of Hamiltonian paths in a tournament on $n$ vertices. We provide our own exposition of these proofs, which were originally found by GPT-5.6.

authors.name: Shouda Wang
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Analyticity of the correlation length in subcritical FK-percolation and Potts models
papers.abstract: We prove that the correlation length of FK-percolation and Potts models on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ is analytic in the whole subcritical regime of parameters. Our proof makes use of the identification of the polar dual of the mass with the solution of an equation involving the leading eigenvalue of the FK--Ruelle operator, introduced in the context of Ornstein--Zernike theory in Campanino, Ioffe and Velenik (Probab. Theory Relat. Fields, 2003), and crucially relies on Kato's theory of analytic perturbation of linear operators. As a consequence of this result, we prove that the correlation length cannot be invariant by rotation except at countably many values of the temperature parameter in the subcritical phase.

authors.name: Lucas D'Alimonte
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: $R$-trivial Galois cohomology classes and cohomological $p$-dimension
papers.abstract: Given a prime $p$, a field $F$ of characteristic different from $p$ and a finite $p$-primary Galois module $V$, a Galois cohomology class in $H^n(F,V)$ is called $R$-trivial if it can be connected to $0$ by a class defined over an open subscheme of the projective line. All classes of $H^n(F,V)$ are $R$-trivial if $F$ has cohomological $p$-dimension at most $n$, by the Bloch-Kato conjecture. We show that this bound is sharp: working over fields of iterated Laurent series, we produce, for every $n\geq 1$, a field $F$ of cohomological $p$-dimension $n+1$ and a Galois module $V$ such that $H^n(F,V)$ contains classes which are not $R$-trivial. The module $V$ is a quotient of the permutation module on the affine hyperplanes of an elementary abelian $p$-group, arising as a quotient of the absolute Galois group of $F$. We also describe $R$-trivial classes as sums of corestrictions of cup products involving a Kummer class.

papers.title: Fluctuations of the planar random walk sausage
papers.abstract: We establish fluctuation results for the volume of random walk sausage $R_n^{A}$ associated to a finite set $A\subset\mathbb{Z}^2$, where the underlying random walk $S$ has finite second moments. Precisely, we establish that the fluctuations are non-Gaussian and are described by the renormalized self intersection local time of planar Brownian motion, as in the cases of the range of random walks and the Wiener sausage. For any $N\ge1$, we also establish an asymptotic expansion of the expected volume of the form \begin{equation*} \mathbb{E}[R_n^{A}]=n\sum_{k=1}^N c(k,A,S)/(\log n)^k+O\left(n/(\log n)^{N+1}\right), \end{equation*} where the constants $c(k,A,S)$ depend only on the order $k$, the set $A$ and the distribution of $S$, and can be computed explicitly in terms of complete exponential Bell polynomials.

papers.title: ScaleRAN: A Runtime for Elastic GPU Resource Management in AI-RAN
papers.abstract: AI-RAN is driving the convergence of radio access network (RAN) processing and artificial intelligence (AI) workloads on GPU-enabled computing platforms, ranging from GPU-accelerated base stations to cloud-native infrastructures. While GPU acceleration improves the efficiency of virtualized RAN functions, the computational demand of latency-critical baseband processing varies with traffic load, creating transient spare GPU capacity that can be reclaimed by co-located AI applications. Existing GPU-sharing mechanisms rely on coarse-grained hardware partitioning or static resource allocation, limiting their ability to adapt to slot-level workload fluctuations while preserving strict timing requirements. This paper presents ScaleRAN, a node-local runtime for elastic GPU resource management in AI-RAN. ScaleRAN leverages NVIDIA Green Contexts to dynamically partition Streaming Multiprocessors (SMs) between RAN and AI workloads through a ladder of pre-created GPU partitions, enabling low-overhead resource reallocation at RAN slot granularity. The proposed runtime naturally supports Open-RAN (O-RAN) O-Cloud deployments, one representative AI-RAN deployment scenario. To drive these reallocations, we propose a reactive controller inspired by Kubernetes autoscaling and a proactive controller based on quantile regression and conformal prediction. We also develop LDPCSim, a GPU-accelerated workload generator built on NVIDIA Aerial for reproducible evaluation. Results show that predictive fine-grained GPU partitioning satisfies slot-level RAN deadlines while increasing the GPU resources available to co-located AI workloads, demonstrating the practicality of elastic GPU sharing for future AI-RAN platforms.

papers.title: Measurement-Adaptive Light-Cone Transform for Robust Non-Line-of-Sight Imaging
papers.abstract: Practical non-line-of-sight (NLOS) measurements are affected by noise and deviations from idealized light transport, which can degrade reconstruction with conventional light-cone transform (LCT) methods. We propose the Measurement-Adaptive Light-Cone Transform (MALCT), a physics-guided framework that retains the efficient Fourier-domain inversion structure of LCT. {Within a unified variational formulation, MALCT combines the analytical response with a shared learned response through measurement-conditioned weighting and predicts a measurement-conditioned, frequency-dependent regularization map.} An attention-enhanced spatio-temporal feature extraction module captures long-range temporal dependencies and local spatial correlations to support reconstruction under low-signal conditions. Experiments on synthetic data and real measurements from different NLOS systems demonstrate improved reconstruction quality. Controlled evaluations further assess robustness to temporal-response broadening and reduced acquisition time. MALCT also preserves scene structures with spatial sampling grids down to $32\times32$, supporting its potential for NLOS imaging under limited acquisition budgets.

authors.name: Lianfang Wang
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

authors.name: Jun Liu
authors.institution: Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China

papers.title: Rigorous verification of period-doubling bifurcations in maps
papers.abstract: We present a computer-assisted approach for proving period-doubling bifurcations in one-parameter families of maps $x \mapsto f(x,λ)$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$. We solve a square augmented system, called the period-doubling map, whose unknowns are the fixed point, the parameter, the right eigenvector attached to the eigenvalue $-1$, the left eigenvector with its eigenvalue, and the vector which describes the center manifold to second order. A contraction argument gives a solution close to a numerical approximation, at which the Jacobian is invertible. The determinant of this Jacobian factors into a simple expression, so that it is nonzero exactly when $1$ is not an eigenvalue and $-1$ is a simple eigenvalue crossing the unit circle transversally. Apart from the sign of the cubic normal-form coefficient, computed afterwards, it remains to check with Gershgorin disks that no other eigenvalue lies on the unit circle. The method is applied to a $10$-mode Galerkin projection of the Kot--Schaffer growth-dispersal model, for which we prove a supercritical period-doubling bifurcation.

papers.title: The Loss or the Architecture? What Matters in Survival Analysis with Competing Risks
papers.abstract: Often, \emph{eg} in healthcare and predictive maintenance, what matters is which of several competing causes will strike first, and with what probability: survival analysis with competing risks. Corresponding deep learning methods are developed as bundles: a new architecture together with a new training loss, tested on one to five datasets against a handful of baselines. Thus, a state-of-the-art result cannot be attributed to the architecture, the loss, or the evaluation protocol. The coupling is not accidental: with one incidence curve per cause, a network's head is tied to the losses expressible on it. We vary the two axes independently, three losses, two of them strictly proper, on four backbones, across two modalities that tease the axes apart: 20 tabular and 3 pathology-image datasets. One loss wins in both: modelling cumulative incidence directly under censoring weighting. It brings twice as much as benefits a good choice of backbone on competing-risks data, and no more than it on single-event data: the loss is decisive for competing risks. The backbone matters too, and must match the modality: tabular networks lead on tables, pretrained vision encoders on images. The two choices compound rather than substitute. Proper scoring rules reveal these dynamics; the concordance index (C-index), which is not proper, does not separate models: neither axis moves it, not even tuning on the loss built to improve it. This is an avenue of progress: composed, the two give a model nobody has tried, RealMLP or TabM trained with the cumulative-incidence loss, which takes the best Brier score in our benchmark.

papers.title: On the Length of Maximum Sum-Rank Distance Codes
papers.abstract: The classical theory of arcs in finite projective spaces provides a powerful geometric framework for studying maximum distance separable (MDS) codes and their possible lengths. In this paper, we investigate how this perspective extends to maximum sum-rank distance (MSRD) codes, whose geometric description involves systems of linear sets rather than individual projective points. Our main goal is to understand how the block structure of an MSRD code constrains its length. In dimension three, we determine the possible intersection patterns of lines with the associated linear sets and obtain explicit formulas for their characters and the weight distribution of the corresponding codes. These results lead to new length bounds and show that the block structure comes at a cost: the presence of a block of rank at least two reduces the maximum possible total length by at least $q-1$, and sufficiently long MSRD codes must be classical, that is, MDS codes over $\mathbb F_{q^m}$. We also prove that three-dimensional one-weight MSRD codes do not exist. In arbitrary dimension, we interpret shortening geometrically as projection and establish a general projection bound that extends classical counting arguments for arcs. This yields restrictions depending explicitly on the block profile and, for full-length blocks, identifies parameter ranges in which linearized Reed--Solomon codes attain the maximum possible number of blocks. Finally, we construct an exceptional three-dimensional MSRD code over $\mathbb F_9$ with three blocks of length two and propose a sum-rank analogue of the MDS conjecture.

papers.title: Borrowing Space, Clustering Temporal Dynamics: Bayesian Regime Mapping and Spatial Prediction for European PM10
papers.abstract: Daily particulate matter measurements from European monitoring networks vary both through spatially shared fluctuations and through differences in local temporal dynamics. Characterising both features is important for identifying groups of monitoring locations with similar temporal behaviour and for predicting concentrations at unmonitored sites. We develop a Bayesian model that combines a continuous spatial common-shock process with a spatial product partition prior for clustering locations according to their local persistence and innovation variability. At unmonitored locations, the model extends these components through spatial interpolation and probabilistic regime allocation. Sparse spatial computations and online prediction summaries make inference feasible for 2,989 monitoring locations and 5,297 unmonitored land locations over 2024. Replicated simulations show that geographic information improves recovery of weakly separated, spatially organised regimes, while uncertainty in regime allocation need not prevent useful continuous prediction. The European analysis identifies stable clusters spanning national boundaries. Clusters with similar persistence nevertheless differ in local innovation variability and in how consistently their stations are grouped together across posterior draws. Comparisons with three restricted models clarify the complementary roles of spatially shared variation, heterogeneous local dynamics and geographic information in the partition.

papers.title: Programming the Nonlinear Optics of a Nanoporous Photonic Metamaterial by Confined Crystallization
papers.abstract: A membrane traversed by a dense array of nanochannels acts as a photonic metamaterial: with channels far smaller than the wavelength of light, the optical response is set by the architecture rather than by the constituent materials. Here each nanochannel is turned into a nonlinear optical meta-atom by filling anodic aluminum oxide (AAO) with benzil (BZL), a noncentrosymmetric molecular crystal, and the crystallization pathway programs their orientation. In free-standing membranes every channel solidifies independently, the orientations remain uncorrelated, and the effective second-harmonic generation (SHG) response is nearly polarization isotropic; its magnitude follows a core - shell model in which an optically inactive interfacial layer of 2.6 nm reduces the active volume of each meta-atom, reproducing on bare alumina the value previously found on alkyl-grafted silica and indicating a host-insensitive limit. Seeding crystallization from a bulk benzil layer instead aligns the meta-atoms over submillimeter domains and produces a macroscopically anisotropic effective susceptibility. Channel diameters from 32 to 270 nm span the transition out of the subwavelength regime, and the anomalous directional SHG emission reported here is confined to the metamaterial limit. Confined crystallization thus offers a route to nonlinear optical metamaterials whose effective susceptibility tensor is written during processing.

authors.name: Yaroslav Shchur
authors.institution: Yukhnovskii Institute for Condensed Matter Physics of the National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine

authors.name: Robert Wielgosz
authors.institution: Bureau international des poids et mesures

papers.title: A Spectral Approach to Fixed Points in Product Spaces
papers.abstract: We study fixed points of mappings on finite products of Banach spaces whose coordinatewise Lipschitz estimates are controlled by a nonnegative matrix $A$. Our main result states that, if every coordinate space has normal structure and $r(A)\leq1$, then every such self-mapping of a nonempty weakly compact convex set has a fixed point. The result is a direct generalization of the Browder--Göhde--Kirk principle. The proof combines classical nonexpansive fixed point theory with Frobenius normal form, passing successively to coordinate projections and invariant fibres. As preparation, the classical reduction of Perov's theorem to the Banach contraction principle through adapted lattice norms is revisited. Applications include a Dirichlet boundary value problem for systems of abstract second order differential equations and a periodic problem for ODE systems satisfying one-sided matrix estimates.

papers.title: When Magnitude Suffices: Reconstructing Time-Domain-Gated Microwave Signals Without Phase on a Thoracic Phantom
papers.abstract: Time-domain gating separates the arrivals that form a microwave S-parameter measurement. It requires the measurement of complex values, so this application almost always uses a vector network analyzer (VNA). We show that, on one calibrated measurement configuration, the gated magnitude the VNA would give can be reconstructed from a magnitude-only sweep of a spectrum analyzer with a tracking generator (SA). We select the gate center for separability of the measured states, correct each instrument once by a per-bin subtraction of a reference state, and train a fully connected network on sweeps from both instruments. The test object is a torso phantom with lung-shaped compartments whose filling takes eleven dielectric states, each held out in turn. On $S_{11}$ the reconstruction from SA input reaches a shape error of 0.08 dB$^2$ with a state ordering of 0.81. This matches the reconstruction from VNA input. On $S_{21}$ it reaches 0.82 dB$^2$ and keeps the ordered groups of the states. An explicit phase prediction performs much worse, because gating needs the phase to about 0.2 rad RMS. Across eleven measurement configurations the dependence of phase on magnitude is strong for reflection and weak for transmission. This explains the difference between $S_{11}$ and $S_{21}$. Where the magnitude carries enough of the phase, a scalar instrument gives the gated response without any phase measurement after installation. On the open UM-BMID breast data set, with whole phantoms held out, the shape error of the network is 30 percent lower than that of a per-bin linear map.

papers.title: CMM-MP: A Novel Memory Pooling Architecture using Purpose-built Memory Device with CXL and Ethernet
papers.abstract: CXL Memory Module - Memory Pooling (CMM-MP) introduces a novel memory pooling architecture to meet the unique requirements of emerging memory-intensive workloads. This industry-first, purpose-built memory-pooling device combines the benefits of Compute Express Link (CXL) with the scalability and cost advantages of Ethernet. Multiple CMM-MP devices together provide a flexible, composable, and disaggregated memory expansion solution. The CMM-MP enables 100s of TB capacity for GPU/CPU applications without modifications. The memory pool is exposed as a large-capacity logical aggregate memory, with all pool discovery, composition, and backend network datapath tasks fully offloaded to the device. CMM-MP supports both memory pooling and sharing usage modes. It provides an application latency of 2.7 us and up to 23 GB/s of memory throughput. Our evaluations demonstrate that CMM-MP significantly outperforms RDMA-based solutions in latency and throughput. We also evaluated real-world use cases of Valkey+YCSB and DiskANN using CMM-MP.

authors.name: Shuyu Lyu
authors.institution: National Taipei University of Nursing and Health Science

authors.name: Xuebin Yao
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics

papers.title: A Minimal ReLU Classifier on Non-Linearly Separable Data: Convergence and Implicit Bias at and beyond the Edge of Stability
papers.abstract: Gradient descent (GD) with large learning rates can successfully optimize neural networks even though classical smoothness-based learning rate conditions are violated. Yet theory for this regime largely covers linear models or linearly separable data. We analyze a minimal setting outside both regimes. Specifically, a two-neuron ReLU network trained with logistic loss on 1D non-linearly separable data. The objective is nonconvex and nonsmooth, and GD exhibits edge-of-stability (EoS) behavior. We identify an active cone in parameter space that contains every perfect classifier, where the problem becomes piecewise logistic regression with a varying effective dataset. Within this cone, we prove a finite-time loss bound for constant learning rates and show that GD converges in direction to an explicit max-margin vector, while the orthogonal component converges to the unique minimizer of a non-strongly convex potential. We further establish catapult results where exponentially small loss is reached after a single loss spike. Furthermore, we propose an adaptive schedule that lets learning rates grow to infinity without leaving the active cone. We prove that this schedule achieves a loss rate of $O(1/(T\log{T})$, which is faster than the standard $O(1/T)$ rate. Our theoretical results extend to local convergence on more general network and are validated on MNIST dataset. Overall, we show that this setup provides a tractable neural-network model for studying large and adaptive step sizes beyond linear predictors and separable data.

authors.name: Robin Yadav
authors.institution: All India Institute of Medical Sciences Rishikesh

authors.name: Mark Schmidt
authors.institution: GEOMAR Helmholtz Centre for Ocean Research Kiel

papers.title: On strongly coherent confidence envelopes for the false discoveries
papers.abstract: Coherence is a long term notion in the literature of multiple testing. From FWER control multiple testing theory to confidence envelopes on the number of false positives, coherence is a desirable property for multiple testing procedures. However, we show in this article that coherence is not a sufficient property to ensure that a multiple testing procedure is nonimprovable via an interpolation mechanism. We introduce a new no- tion, the notion of strong coherence, which is a stronger property than coherence and ensures that a multiple testing procedure is nonimprovable via the interpolation mech- anisms considered in the literature. Finally, we provide a uniform improvement of the confidence envelope from Durand et al. (2020) that is computable in polynomial time and demonstrate the improvement on simulated data.

authors.name: Guillermo Durand
authors.institution: Consejo Nacional de Investigaciones Científicas y Técnicas

papers.title: Regular Additive Scalar Invariants of ${\mathcal N}=1$ Hyperbolic Spin Supertriangles
papers.abstract: We classify regular cyclic scalar invariants of non-degenerate hyperbolic ${\mathcal N}=1$ spin supertriangles which are additive under geodesic subdivision. After fixing the spin lift, the common-first gauge (introduced in earlier work by the second-named author and further developed here) gives a complete $3|4$ modulus of such supertriangles.. The space of additive scalar invariants is proved to have superdimension $3|1$: ordinary hyperbolic area in degree zero, two even generators in degree two, and one odd generator in degree three; the degree-one and degree-four sectors vanish. One degree-two generator is the fermionic first variation of body area, equivalently the nilpotent correction from ordinary body angle defect to super angle defect. The degree-three generator changes sign under reversal of the spin lift, while the other generators are fixed, so ordinary supertriangles carry only three even invariants.

papers.title: NLData2Opt: Benchmarking Parameter Derivation and Prediction for Modeling Optimization Problems from Natural Language and Data
papers.abstract: Formulating optimization problems from raw inputs of problem descriptions and data is time-consuming and costly. While Large Language Models (LLMs) offer a promising way to automate this process, existing benchmarks overestimate their capabilities by relying on idealized inputs where all data is relevant and complete. This diverges from reality, where data-centric reasoning is required to extract, compute, and predict parameters from noisy sources. To address this, we introduce NLData2Opt, a benchmark to evaluate LLMs on the multi-stage reasoning inherent in practical optimization workflows. NLData2Opt decomposes problems into problem descriptions and data, and requires models to (1) extract relevant parameters from data containing misleading attributes, (2) compute missing parameters derived by transforming existing data attributes, and (3) predict unavailable future values from historical observations. Evaluation results show substantial performance decline relative to existing benchmarks, indicating that benchmark progress does not directly translate to formulation accuracy in practical optimization workflows. NLData2Opt is available at https://github.com/sumarivyn/NLData2Opt.

authors.name: Kyohei Atarashi
authors.institution: SODA: Méthodes computationnelles et mathématiques pour comprendre la société et la santé à partir de données

authors.name: Hisashi Kashima
authors.institution: SODA: Méthodes computationnelles et mathématiques pour comprendre la société et la santé à partir de données

papers.title: On the possibilities and limitations of LLM-based multi-agent systems for multi-criteria decision-making in healthcare operations management
papers.abstract: Multi-criteria models for healthcare operations need weights that express how stakeholders trade off patient waiting time, provider workload, and operating cost, but these weights are difficult to quantify. Teams of large language model (LLM) agents, each prompted to represent a stakeholder, have been used to supply them. We propose a framework for assessing the reliability of LLM-generated preferences as inputs to multi-objective optimization and quantifying how their uncertainty affects decisions. We study explicit preferences by asking agents to rate the importance of the criteria in an outpatient appointment scheduling problem, and implicit preferences by inferring trade-offs from the agents' pairwise choices between emergency department configurations. The computational experiments show that the explicit preferences respond to the clinic's operating conditions and differ across roles, but deliberation among the agents can erase these differences, whereas simple averaging preserves them. The pairwise choices used to reveal the agents' implicit preferences depend largely on which option is presented first, and we find limited evidence that a statistical model using contextual information alongside presentation order predicts the agents' choices on new comparison pairs better than a model using presentation order alone. We then formulate robust weighted-sum optimization models to account for preference uncertainty. In most cases, these models select different schedules or configurations from those obtained using average preference weights. These results indicate that LLM-generated preferences need an audit of this kind before they are used as optimization weights in healthcare decision support.

authors.name: Marco Boresta
authors.institution: Istituto di Analisi dei Sistemi ed Informatica Antonio Ruberti

papers.title: Absolute continuity of invariant measures for random diffeomorphisms
papers.abstract: We develop criteria showing that invariant measures for random walks generated by diffeomorphisms of manifolds are in the Lebesgue class. Our assumptions are first, that there is a uniform expansion gap in the Lyapunov spectrum of the random walk, and second, that the conditionals of the invariant measure along the appropriate (partial) stable manifolds are in the Lebesgue class.

papers.title: Rational decomposition of polyhedra and a conjecture of Brlek and Reutenauer
papers.abstract: We prove in the affirmative a conjecture of Brlek and Reutenauer (2003), which relates unambiguous rational sets to a well known result due to Khovanskii and Pukhlikov (1992) and independently to Lawrence (1990) on the valuations of the algebra spanned by the indicator functions of polyhedra.

papers.title: What It Is, Not What It Says: Securing Agentic Browsing Interactions with Web Semantics
papers.abstract: AI agents increasingly browse the web on users' behalf, yet they consume webpages as screenshots or text, exposing their LLMs to unvetted third-party content. Browsers enforce semantics under which what an element can do depends on what it is and where it comes from, not on what it says. Agents flatten these semantics, so injected text can persuade the LLM to exercise the user's authority for content that has none. As LLMs remain easy to persuade, the agent's interface to the web must itself ensure the integrity of what the agent reads, interprets, and does. We propose Intact, which runs on an unmodified browser. Intact builds GenTree, a bespoke representation that captures provenance and web semantics. Intact passes the page via GenTree to the LLM one element at a time, so the LLM decides on each element without any other element's text. Its harness executes each step only within the capabilities of the step's element and asks the user before acting on third-party content. On 1,270 real webpages, GenTree attributes 2.3x as many elements to third parties as the browser, which misattributes 58.7% of them to the first party. On 1,091 of these webpages with injected attacks, only 12.8% of attacks get through Intact's planner, each at most as a consent request, against 73.1% for a conventional planner. Isolation disrupts functionality on only 3.7% of tasks, and a parallel schedule could remove most of its added latency.

papers.title: Prospects for Simultaneously Detecting Long and Short Duration Gravitational Waves from Pulsar Glitches with Current and Future Detectors
papers.abstract: The internal mechanisms that drive the sudden change in rotation frequency in pulsar glitches could emit gravitational waves (GWs) at multiple time scales. The potential for GW analyses to detect both long and short forms of emission ("tCW-like" and "burst-like") improves as the detectors increase in sensitivity. We aim to examine how future detectors fare in making this joint measurement. By examining past glitches from the ATNF catalog, we quantify the double-detectability prospects of current- and next-generation GW detector networks. We further explore what astrophysical constraints could be placed following a double non-detection using extrapolations from the 2024 Vela pulsar glitch as a stand-in example. We find that a network with at least one next-generation detector greatly increases the probability of double-detection for many known glitching pulsars and improves the detection threshold in glitch energy by nearly two orders of magnitude over existing LIGO detectors. Additionally, double non-detections with networks with at least one next-generation detector could place dramatically improved limits on properties of the pulsar.

papers.title: Hypercube Richardson varieties from magic words
papers.abstract: Inspired by the recent preprint of Ellenberg, Libedinsky, Plaza, Simental, and Williamson, we study the geometry of Richardson varieties whose associated Bruhat intervals are boolean posets. We define magic words for a Bruhat interval and prove that for intervals with magic words the associated Richardson variety is a tower of $\mathbb{P}^1$-s. We also prove that the Bruhat intervals consisting of the dyadically well-distributed permutations all have magic words. This gives a new proof that they form a boolean poset.

papers.title: Exotic symplectomorphisms of strong fillings
papers.abstract: We prove a criterion for detecting exotic symplectomorphisms of strong fillings of closed contact manifolds. The criterion concerns symplectomorphisms induced by free contact circle actions on the boundary, and it is expressed purely in topological terms. As an application, we show that one-point blow-ups of an infinite family of Brieskorn varieties admit exotic compactly supported symplectomorphisms.

papers.title: A note on the non-wandering dynamics in the $n$-fold symmetric products
papers.abstract: We construct a homeomorphism on a compact metric space whose non-wandering set consists of a single fixed point, while the induced map $F_n(f)$ possesses infinitely many (non-fixed) non-wandering points.

authors.name: Maša Đorić
authors.institution: Mathematical Institute of the Serbian Academy of Sciences and Arts

papers.title: Cryptographically Secure Agent-to-Agent Communication in Multi-Agent Systems
papers.abstract: Multi-agent systems (MAS) comprise AI agents that collaborate or compete to perform complex, distributed tasks. Their dynamic interactions create opportunities for threat actors to target and impersonate other agents, intercept messages, inject malicious prompts, and exfiltrate sensitive data while simultaneously complicating the detection of anomalous behavior through conventional monitoring. This paper surveys threats and cryptographic challenges in agent-to-agent communication and presents a zero-trust architecture integrating identity, transport security, message integrity, and monitoring. The architecture establishes agent identities via decentralized identifiers and task-scoped verifiable credentials backed by a permissioned ledger, enforcing least-privilege authorization. For transport security, it provides mutually authenticated, crypto-agile TLS with hybrid post-quantum key establishment, and evaluates KEMTLS with pre-distributed public keys to reduce handshake overhead. Signed CBOR envelopes preserve payload integrity across multi-hop exchanges, while zero-knowledge proofs verify declared task constraints without exposing underlying inputs. Context-aware monitoring of inter-agent messages, tool activity, and execution telemetry informs the setting of risk-based trust thresholds and supports the detection of behavioral anomalies. Together, these mechanisms provide an integrated framework for securing and auditing agent communication, with implications for other agentic protocols and prospective 6G semantic communication.

papers.title: Stability of Hyperplane Projections of the Regular Simplex and $L_p$-Projection Bodies of balls in $\ell_q^n(\mathbb{R})$
papers.abstract: We prove stability estimates for extremal hyperplane projections of the regular simplex. We further generalize the analogous stability estimates for $\ell_q$-balls by the first named author and the monotonicity theorem for normalized ratios by Barthe and Naor to the $L_p$-setting. To this end, we derive closed formulas for the support functions of their $L_p$-projection bodies, complementing those obtained by the second named author. A key ingredient in our proofs is a stability refinement of the majorization inequality for Gaussian mixtures.

papers.title: The Sign Code: The Hidden Binary Nature of Deep Networks
papers.abstract: Every neuron in a trained network outputs a number that can be separated into its sign (positive or negative) and its magnitude (absolute size). We call the set of all neuron signs the \textit{sign code}. This raises a key question: does classification depend more on the sign code or on the magnitudes? For overparameterized vision classifiers with sign-preserving activations, the answer is overwhelmingly the sign code. A $k$-nearest neighbor classifier operating only on this binary sign code achieves accuracy comparable to the full model across different architectures, activation functions, and datasets. Moreover, replacing all magnitudes in every layer with random noise while keeping the original signs barely changes residual network performance. In contrast, flipping just 20\% of the signs reduces accuracy to chance. Models generalize well when same-class inputs share similar sign codes. When this overlap is disrupted by a regularizer, training accuracy remains high, but test performance collapses. A margin decomposition helps explain these results: the sign-only contribution to each logit grows as $\sqrt{d}$ in network width, dominating the magnitude residual. The natural unit of analysis for these networks may not be through their continuous weight space but instead through their discrete sign codes.

papers.title: Escaping Parameter Space: Tight Generalization Bounds via Representation Quality
papers.abstract: We derive a tight generalization bound for deterministic neural We derive a tight generalization bound for deterministic neural networks based on their last hidden layer representations. By evaluating representation quality with a parameter-free $k$-nearest-neighbor ($k$-NN) classifier, our certificate avoids traditional parameter-space complexity measures, KL divergences to a posterior, weight norms, and compression. The bound is tight: trained from scratch, it reaches an 8.0 percentage point gap to test error on CIFAR-10 (ResNet-18) and yields the first non-vacuous certificates we are aware of on CIFAR-100; with frozen DINOv2 representations, it certifies at 1.4\% on CIFAR-10 and 23.1\% on 1,000-class ImageNet. It decomposes additively into three empirical, independently measurable quantities: local class geometry ($k$-NN decoder error), decoder-network agreement, and training stability. This allows the bound to act as a diagnostic tool: we demonstrate that actively destroying local class geometry eliminates generalization while leaving dataset memorization intact, identifying class geometry as a causally relevant mechanism for generalization. Finally, we show that learned representations are significantly less sensitive to weight noise than linear readouts, suggesting why parameter-space certificates often struggle to remain tight.

papers.title: Low-weight compactly supported cohomology of $\mathcal M_{g,n}^{ct}$ and the extended Torelli morphism
papers.abstract: We study the weight zero and weight two graded pieces of the compactly supported cohomology of the moduli space $\mathcal M_{g,n}^{ct}$ of stable $n$-pointed curves of genus $g$ of compact type and show that they are computed by bridgeless graph complexes. In weight two, we construct a natural embedding of shifted weight zero cohomology from lower genus. For unmarked curves, we construct canonical classes represented by pinched odd wheel graphs and prove that distinct wheel monomials give linearly independent classes in the dual of $W_0H_c^{2g}(\mathcal M_g^{ct};\mathbb Q)$. By relating the bridgeless graph complex to the $K$-theory of graphs and the Quillen spectral sequence, we show that these classes remain linearly independent after pushforward along the extended Torelli morphism $\mathcal M_g^{ct}\to\mathcal A_g$. Finally, we prove that the realizations of the motivic Lie algebra arising from $\mathcal M_g$ and $\mathcal A_g$ have the same image in the weight zero compactly supported cohomology of $\mathcal M_g^{ct}$.

papers.title: A Topological Signature of Learning under Noisy Labels
papers.abstract: How does noisy supervision change the representations learned by a neural network? Training accuracy measures agreement with training labels but provides little information about representation geometry. We use persistent homology to track loop structure across distance thresholds in neural activations. Experiments span image classification, text classification, and modular arithmetic. On a fixed CIFAR-10/ResNet-18 training probe, equally sized clean-label and corrupted-label subsets show no detectable persistence difference at epoch 10, whereas corrupted-label subsets have higher persistence at epoch 50. The contrast survives uniform-scale controls, even though predictions match the assigned noisy labels for only 7-11% of corrupted probe examples at that checkpoint. Normalisation preserves the crossover between clean and noisy training trajectories on CIFAR-10/ResNet-18, whereas CIFAR-100/ResNet-18 shows no crossover under any of the five evaluated constructions. In a separate noise-rate calibration comparison across five pipelines, mean activation norm achieves a higher mean in-sample R2 than raw persistence (0.936 versus 0.908). These findings show that noisy supervision leaves a measurable geometric signature even when agreement with corrupted labels is low. Comparing persistence under scale controls with label-fitting measurements offers a way to study how representations respond to label corruption beyond what training accuracy reveals.

papers.title: Recognizing Study Lineage Is Not Enough: Over-Crediting Same-Trial Evidence in LLM-Based Medical Verification
papers.abstract: Publication count is not study count. A model can identify shared trial lineage correctly in a direct task yet over-credit a second publication from the same trial when aggregating evidence. We evaluate this behavior in medical LLM verification using 14 source-audited clinical families and five model conditions. The families span provenance, clinical applicability, result direction, and composition; the provenance families provide the direct lineage tests. Recognition and aggregation are separate stateless calls, and repeated calls assess within-input stability. Across all three original provenance families, GPT-5.5 identifies the independent update in 10/10 recognition calls per family but over-credits the same-trial report in 5/5 separate aggregation calls per family. Selected Qwen3-4B and Ministral-3-8B conditions show the same cross-task contrast. A study-grouping instruction reduces GPT-5.5 over-credit from 4/5 to 0/5 in each later pure-provenance family. Other model conditions show mixed behavior, and rejected outputs limit several comparisons. The results identify a behavioral gap between elicited lineage recognition and evidence aggregation. The code and data artifacts are available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/study-lineage-review-artifact.

papers.title: Non-Parametric Optimization for Scalable Learning in Stochastic Decision Problems
papers.abstract: Stochastic optimization (SO) plays a central role in decision-making under uncertainty. Among SO problems, time-varying stochastic optimization (TV-SO) is particularly important due to its applications in adaptive control and machine learning. Non-parametric approaches have been proposed for time-varying deterministic optimization; however, they have not been developed for their stochastic counterparts. This work addresses that gap by developing a stochastic variational framework based on Malliavin calculus. This framework yields non-parametric optimality conditions for SO problems with stochastic decisions and supports the design of a scalable deep-learning algorithm that is insensitive to the parameterization dimension. This algorithm, called the Stochastic Path Follower (SPF), is applied to two important problems under distribution drift, namely least-squares recovery and logistic regression. Experimental results show that the proposed approach outperforms state-of-the-art learning-based and gradient-based methods in both performance and scalability.

papers.title: From Billion-Scale to Million-Scale Language Models: Operational Capabilities for Embedded Post-Exploitation
papers.abstract: Small Language Models (SLMs) are increasingly attractive for resource-constrained environments due to their low computational footprint. These characteristics also make them candidates for future autonomous malware, where connectivity, latency, privacy, or operational constraints may preclude cloud-based inference. Yet the ability of ultra-compact models to support malware during post-exploitation remains poorly understood. We systematically evaluate seven open-source SLMs (20M-1.5B parameters) on two post-exploitation code-generation tasks: Directory Enumeration and Backdoor Generation. We compare Python (high-resource) and Lua (low-resource) across prompting strategies, task formulations, iterative reasoning, grammar-constrained decoding, and execution-feedback loops. Results show that offensive code-generation capabilities do not increase linearly with model size. Successful execution depends on the interaction of model capacity, task formulation, and prompting strategy, with task formulation exerting a greater influence than prompt engineering alone. Algorithmic formulation combined with few-shot prompting enables Qwen2.5-Coder 1.5B to reach Pass@5 of 100% in both Python and Lua for Directory Enumeration, 100% in Python for Backdoor Generation, and 99.2% in Lua. Although the evaluated models remain too computationally demanding for widespread deployment in contemporary malware, rapid progress in compact models may reduce this barrier. These findings help anticipate AI-assisted malware and inform future countermeasures.

papers.title: $a$-numbers of covers in characteristic two: semigroups and Riemann-Roch spaces
papers.abstract: We compute the $a$-numbers of the Garcia-Güneri-Stichtenoth curves, the Beelen-Montanucci curves, and the Skabelund covers of Suzuki curves in characteristic two. The proofs use the identity $a(X)=\ell(\tfrac12\operatorname{div}(dt))$ and reduce the calculations to Riemann-Roch spaces on the base curves. We obtain transfer formulas for odd-degree radical covers, with one or several points at infinity, and evaluate them using Weierstrass semigroups and plane sections of the Hermitian curve. For the first two families we also give cyclic models over the projective line and relate the formulas to Elkin's rank formula. We then treat two classes of Artin-Schreier fibre products. A supersingular genus-six family has a-number $3$ at the zero parameter and $2$ elsewhere, although the genera and $a$-numbers of its quadratic quotients remain fixed. We determine its Ekedahl--Oort types as $(0,0,0,1,2,3)$ and $(0,1,1,2,3,4)$,

authors.name: Saeed Tafazolian
authors.institution: Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare, Sezione di Napoli

papers.title: Nonlocal-to-local variational limits of energies on partitions
papers.abstract: We study, through a $Γ$-convergence procedure, the asymptotic behaviour of a general class of nonlocal energies defined on functions taking values in a finite set $Y=\{y_1,\dots,y_N\}\subset\mathbb R^m$. These energies are written in terms of double integrals accounting for pairwise interactions in an open set $Ω$, weighted by a kernel $K_\varepsilon$. If the latter is controlled from above and below by suitable non-negative radial kernels with unit mass concentrating at the origin, then, up to subsequences, the $Γ$-limit has domain $BV(Ω;Y)$ and is given by a local surface energy. We show that the locality of the $Γ$-limit is not guaranteed if the concentration of mass fails. For a class of reference energies, we obtain a more explicit representation of the limit energy, also for non-radial kernels, recovering the limits of isotropic and anisotropic fractional perimeters. We also prove a homogenization result for periodic kernels.

papers.title: Learning Robot Metareasoning: Adaptive Computation Budgets for Real-Time Control
papers.abstract: Planning while moving faces an historical trade-off between deliberation and reactivity. A planner running concurrently with execution needs time to compute, so the robot must commit to an open-loop action chunk for that duration: a longer commitment buys a better plan at the cost of feedback frequency. Existing controllers fix this action commitment, and consequently the computation budget, before deployment. However, the optimal computation time is highly state-dependent (due to factors such as unmodeled dynamics, safety constraints, and marginal optimisation gains), i.e. dynamic, therefore offline static tuning risks leaving systems blind during critical maneuvers or unable to find global effective solutions. We cast the identification of the optimal computation budget as a semi-Markov decision process (SMDP) in which a single decision defines both the robot action commitments and the time allocated to the solver. To solve this, we train a reinforcement-learning policy conditioned on the current state, the executing plan, and inexpensive planner statistics. Across ground-robot navigation, agile quadrotor flight, and contact-rich manipulation, the learned policy changes its budget with the demands of the scenario, discovering efficient reasoning patterns that outperform fixed-budget baselines. https://lorenzomagnino.github.io/learning-robot-metareasoning-review/

papers.title: Weakly Supervised Discovery of Motion Styles for Compositional Robot Control
papers.abstract: When a robot possesses more degrees of freedom than a task requires, multiple trajectories can achieve the same objective using distinct motion styles. Compositional robot control aims to preserve a selected style while simultaneously executing an independent task command, effectively balancing these potentially competing objectives. In this paper, we present CODES, a framework for compositional robot control that discovers a coherent style repertoire from diverse recordings and composes it with independent commands. First, motion retargeting maps the recordings to motions executable by the target robot; next, weakly supervised consensus encoding and density-based clustering identify styles within and across recordings without a prescribed count; finally, reinforcement learning trains a policy to compose the discovered styles with independent commands. We evaluate CODES on a Unitree Go2 quadruped across two simulators and physical hardware. Compared to baselines, CODES significantly improves kinematic coherence. Furthermore, our controller successfully tracks velocity commands that generalize beyond the support of the recorded data, exhibiting robust and distinguishable style characteristics during both cross-simulator and real-world hardware deployments. Project website: https://www.proroklab.org/compositional-motion-styles/

papers.title: An improved randomized algorithm for finding sinks of Acyclic Unique Sink Orientations of the binary hypercube
papers.abstract: Acyclic Unique Sink Orientations (AUSOs) of the binary hypercube form an elegant abstraction of various optimization problems, ranging from linear programs whose feasibility region is a combinatorial hypercube, to 2-player turn-based stochastic games (2TBSGs) in which one of the players has two actions from each one of its states. The currently fastest known randomized algorithm for finding the sink of such AUSOs is the Random-Facet algorithm of Kalai (STOC 1992), and of Matoušek, Sharir and Welzl (SoCG 1992), adapted to the binary hypercube by Gärtner (RSA 2002). The expected number of vertex queries made by the algorithm is at most $e^{2\sqrt{n}}$, where $n$ is the dimension of the cube. We design an improved randomized sink-finding algorithm that performs an expected number of only $e^{\sqrt{(2+o(1))n}}$ queries. This is the first improved bound for the problem in over two decades. The improved algorithm is obtained by adapting improved versions of the Random-Facet algorithm for solving general linear programs, and LP-type problems, developed by Kalai (STOC 1992), Gärtner (FOCS 1992), and by Hansen and Zwick (STOC 2015). The improved bound is not implied by these much more general algorithms. A key feature of the improved algorithm and its analysis is its simplicity. The structure of binary AUSOs enables a simpler description and a much simpler analysis of the adapted algorithm. In particular, the recurrence relations bounding the complexity of the algorithm depend on only one variable, and not two, and they can be solved using fairly straightforward techniques.

papers.title: NoveltyScope: A Multi-Agent Research Assistant for Evidence-Grounded Novelty Assessment of Scientific Papers
papers.abstract: NoveltyScope is a prototype that compares a scientific paper with retrieved prior work and produces a structured report and a five-level novelty score. The system extracts the core task and at most two author-claimed contributions, then searches a closed local corpus using BM25 and dense retrieval with reciprocal rank fusion. Contribution comparisons request paired passages for potential refutations, and quotations are checked against cached source text. Four scoring roles (Prosecutor, Defender, Judge, and Critic) use the resulting evidence, with at most one revision of the Judge's score. Evaluation uses 50 class-balanced RINoBench samples whose idea-level labels are retained for full-paper input. Mean absolute error is 1.48 and 1.26 for single-LLM and multi-agent scoring with Gemini, respectively, and 1.22 and 1.16 with Qwen3. The vector-similarity baseline has an error of 1.68. A HiCLIP case study illustrates the contribution comparisons and paired evidence passages. Overall, the results demonstrate the feasibility of evidence-grounded novelty assessment and show that the multi-agent configurations achieve lower scoring errors than their single-LLM counterparts across both evaluated models.

papers.title: Can AI interview? Comparing AI-led to Human-led Chat Interviews
papers.abstract: Large language model chatbots have been proposed as AI-interviewers for collecting qualitative interview data at scale, potentially bridging social science's longstanding divide between the breadth of surveys and the depth of qualitative interviews. This paper provides the first direct empirical comparison of data quality in AI-led and human-led interviews. In a randomized experiment (N = 41), university students were interviewed via synchronous text chat by either trained non-expert interviewers or a locally hosted AI system; we evaluate exposure, specificity, and relevance. Median interview duration was similar across conditions, but AI-interviewers asked more than twice as many questions per interview and elicited roughly 65 percent more respondent text per interview. Per-question responses were longer with human interviewers, though not after multiple-testing correction; only AI-condition participants skipped questions. Responses were almost uniformly on-topic in both conditions; for specificity we detect no difference, but the design cannot exclude one of up to three quarters of a point. These results were obtained with a small, locally hosted open-weight model (7B parameters), which addresses concerns about data security, GDPR compliance, and scientific reproducibility. Our findings support the viability of AI-interviewing for large-N qualitative data collection.

papers.title: A Structure-Preserving Semi-Lagrangian based bi-fidelity method for the Vlasov--Poisson system with uncertainties
papers.abstract: Uncertainty quantification for the Vlasov--Poisson (VP) systems entails repeated dynamic simulations, incurring immense computational costs. We develop a structure-preserving Semi-Lagrangian (SL) b-fidelity approximation of macroscopic observables. The MUSCL is used as a low-fidelity solver for pressureless Euler--Poisson system, allowing for a more cost-effective exploration of the stochastic parameter space. A conservative SL scheme combined with high-order discontinuous Galerkin is used as a high-fidelity solver for collisionless VP system, whose mass conservation, positivity preservation, and low numerical dissipation provide a more reliable high-fidelity snapshots for bi-fidelity reconstruction. We further derive a conditional error bound that separates projection, discretization, and model errors. Numerical experiments for both deterministic and uncertain VP problems, including multispecies and higher-dimensional settings, demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves accurate and robust uncertainty propagation.

authors.name: Xiaofeng Cai
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: An Erdős-Pósa theorem for induced packings of even cycles
papers.abstract: We show that for every graph $G$ and every positive integer $k$, $G$ contains either $k$ vertex-disjoint even cycles with no edges between distinct cycles, or a set of $O(k^2\log k)$ vertices whose closed neighborhood meets every even cycle of $G$. Moreover, we give a polynomial-time algorithm that outputs one of the two outcomes. As an application, we show that every $K_{1,t}$-free graph containing no induced packing of $k$ even cycles has tree-independence number $O(tk^2\log k)$, with a corresponding decomposition computable in polynomial time.

papers.title: MLLM Frame Subset Ensembling for Audio-Visual Video QA and MLLM-based Reranking for Ad-hoc Video Search in TRECVID 2025
papers.abstract: This paper presents the overview of the runs related to the Ad-hoc Video Search (AVS) and Video Question Answering (VQA) tracks of TRECVID 2025 on behalf of the CERTH-ITI team. For the AVS track, we introduce a two-stage framework built on foundation models. In the first stage, multiple vision-language models (VLMs) encode both the input query, augmented through LLM-generated rephrasings, and the candidate video shots, producing weighted similarity scores for initial retrieval. In the second stage, we utilize a Multimodal-LLM(MLLM)-based reranking module that evaluates the semantic alignment between each shot among the top-N highest-ranked ones and the original query, generating updated relevance scores for reordering these shots. This MLLM-driven reranking significantly improves contextual matching and produces more accurate final rankings without requiring any model training. Regarding the VQA track, we fine-tune an audio-visual MLLM model on the provided TRECVID training dataset and we implement an inference-time scaling technique to enhance the multimodal understanding capabilities of the MLLM. For the open-ended Answer Generation (AG) task, we aggregate multiple model responses per question via a majority vote. The responses are generated with greedy sampling from different random frame subsets of the video and they are ranked based on the number of votes. For the Multiple-Choice (MC) task, instead of voting, we use mean pooling on the logits assigned by the fine-tuned model to each candidate response. Through the combination of fine-tuning and frame subset ensembling we achieve the highest score across 3 metrics in the VQA AG task and the second highest in the VQA MC task.

papers.title: CLEAR: Cooperative Latent Flow for Visual Counterfactual Explanations with Accurate Region Preservation
papers.abstract: Visual counterfactual explanations (VCEs) should alter a classifier's prediction while remaining realistic and preserving decision-irrelevant content. Image-space methods provide high-quality counterfactuals but are computationally costly, whereas latent-space methods are more efficient but often less faithful. We identify two sources responsible for this gap. First, latent generation recovers a natural sample from a perturbed representation, whereas classifier guidance pushes it toward a target class, so their update directions may oppose. Second, VAE reconstruction can alter regions that should remain unchanged. We introduce CLEAR, a latent Flow Matching framework for VCEs. CLEAR uses Flow Matching's explicit instantaneous velocity as a reference for the generative direction to decompose classifier guidance into cooperative and conflicting components. It preserves the cooperative component and adaptively attenuates only the conflicting one according to conflict strength. We further analyze conflict frequency and strength throughout generation to reveal how classifier guidance interacts with the generative process. CLEAR also dynamically identifies editable regions, constrains latent modifications, and directly preserves factual content outside them to reduce VAE-induced changes. Across five bidirectional tasks on two datasets, CLEAR retains latent-space efficiency while achieving counterfactual quality comparable to or better than strong image-space baselines, with a 2.5x speedup over the strongest baseline. Project page: https://yan-zen9.github.io/CLEAR/

papers.title: AcupunctureBench: A Multimodal Benchmark for Evaluating Generative Models in the Acupuncture Domain
papers.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied in the field of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), standardized benchmark evaluations for TCM have gradually emerged. Acupuncture is a crucial component of TCM. However, existing evaluation benchmarks are lacking in this domain. To address this gap, this paper proposes AcupunctureBench, the first independently constructed large-scale multimodal benchmark for the acupuncture domain, covering text, image, and video modalities. The AcupunctureBench spans multidimen sional knowledge in acupuncture, including acupuncture theory, meridians and acupoints, clinical reasoning, TCM syndromes, and practical acupoint operation. To achieve large-scale construction while ensuring medical professionalism, this work designs a human-machine collaborative data construction pipeline and proposes efficient deduplication strategies to reduce redundant samples, while extensively adopting data synthesis to mitigate data leak age risks. AcupunctureBench contains a total of 58,526 question samples and 1,216 video samples, covering multiple task types including objective questions, subjective question answering, case analysis, image understanding, image reasoning, and video understanding. Based on this benchmark, this paper evaluates 14 large language models, 14 large multimodal models, and 4 video foundation models, and further releases the first dedicated evaluation website for the acupuncture domain.

authors.name: Xingfang Pan
authors.institution: Tianjin University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

authors.name: Yangyang Liu
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Bayesian Geophysical Inversion using Stein Mixture Variational Inference for Multimodal or Complex Solutions
papers.abstract: Bayesian geophysical inversion provides a probabilistic framework to estimate subsurface properties, in which uncertainties are represented by a so-called posterior probability density function (pdf). Estimating this pdf is computationally challenging when it is high dimensional or complex, particularly if it may be multimodal. We introduce Stein mixture variational inference (SMVI) for efficient Bayesian geophysical inversion with multimodal or complex posterior solutions. The method combines parametric variational inference with Stein variational gradient descent (SVGD). In SMVI, the posterior pdf is approximated by a mixture (sum) of distributions, in which component distributions are optimised jointly using the SVGD update rule. This construction combines computational efficiency with the flexibility to represent a range of plausible Earth models and allows components to be updated in parallel. Here, SMVI is first tested on two synthetic seismic inverse problems, demonstrating that SMVI can recover non-Gaussian, complex and multimodal posterior solutions accurately and efficiently. Then, we apply SMVI to real seismic data by performing Love wave tomography of the British Isles, and obtain inversion results that are consistent with previous Monte Carlo solutions. Around the East Irish Sea sedimentary basins, SMVI captures bimodal uncertainty associated with ambiguity in basin boundary locations, revealing alternative subsurface structures compatible with the observations. These results indicate that SMVI generalises various previous variational methods, and provides a practical and effective framework for quantifying complex uncertainties and supporting geological interpretation of seismic images.

papers.title: On the two critical exponents for a dispersive equation with weak dissipation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study a nonlinear Cauchy problem written in normal form \begin{equation*} \begin{cases} u_{tt} + A u+ Bu_t =D|u|^α, & t\geq 0, x \in \mathbb{R}^n\\ u(0,x)=u_0(x),\,u_t(0,x)=u_1(x). \end{cases} \end{equation*} Here~ $Af=\mathscr{F}^{-1}(a(ξ)^2\mathscr{F}f)$, with $a(ξ)$ homogeneous of order $k > 0$ under the assumption that the Hessian matrix of $a(ξ)$ is nonsingular, the operator $Bf=\mathscr{F}^{-1}(b(ξ)\mathscr{F}f)$ represents a weak dissipation, in the sense that $b(ξ) \sim 1$ as $|ξ| \to \infty$ and %, in several models, $D=B$ but we also consider the case $Df=ν\ast (-Δ)^δ(I-Δ)^{-δ}$, with $ν$ a bounded measure and $δ\geq k/2$. We derive $L^p-L^q$ estimates of the linear solution operator to the considered model and we prove the transition from a Fujita-type exponent to a Strauss-type exponent for the global-in-time existence of small data solution for the corresponding nonlinear problems.

papers.title: The Window Is in the Reasoning: When LLM Agents Decide to Follow Prompt Injections
