papers.title: PresenceBench: An Exploratory Evaluation of Large Language Model Adaptation to User State
papers.abstract: Presence-aware intelligence is the capacity of an AI system's intelligence layer to adapt appropriately to the functional state of the person it serves (here readiness, flow, and stability) while preserving task quality and safety. We introduce PresenceBench, an instrument for measuring it. PresenceBench evaluates how the intelligence layer uses a supplied state, not how that state is sensed, and breaks the capability into measurable properties. Two are tested here. Receptivity: does the model take up the state and give a better response than with no signal? Specificity: does any improvement depend on the correct state, rather than on extra structured context? A third, adaptation across states, is a required endpoint not measured in this release. A five-arm causal design answers both questions, against each model's own baseline and an equally structured mismatched-state control, scored by a correctness-gated human paired comparison. The exploratory evaluation covered four models across eighteen single-turn, six fixed three-turn and six simulated natural-conversation scenarios. Supplying a synthetic state, raw or translated into a response policy, gave human-preference point estimates above 0.5 for all four models (Claude Sonnet 5, DeepSeek V4 Pro, Gemini 3.6 Flash, GPT-5.6 Terra), with three of eight 95% intervals excluding chance. Specificity was not resolved: no per-model interval excluded chance, and the design cannot yet separate the state values from a generic instruction to adapt. Policy delivery reduced priced cost and output tokens against each model's baseline; these are resource-use changes, not efficiency gains, because correctness non-inferiority was not established. Safety-floor failures were rare (13 of 360 cases), with a non-significant excess under policy delivery. We report the instrument, the frozen results, and the controls a confirmatory study needs.

papers.title: A Topological Quantum Field Theory for Representation Varieties of Torus Links
papers.abstract: We construct a Topological Quantum Field Theory (TQFT) that computes the virtual classes of $G$-representation varieties associated with the fundamental group of a torus link complement. Following the framework established by González-Prieto, Logares and Muñoz for $G$-representation varieties of surface groups, we introduce a suitable bordism whose iteration enables a recursive topological evaluation of these virtual classes. Via this TQFT, we explicitly compute the virtual class of these varieties for the groups $G=\mathrm{AGL}_1(\mathbb{C})$ and $G=\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$.

papers.title: On extremal problems related to the Krzyż conjecture
papers.abstract: We study general extremal problems similar or closely related to the Krzyż conjecture and establish the structural properties of extremal functions, pointing out some differences with the original Krzyż case. We also introduce a family of more specific problems of this kind, interpolating between the Krzyż problem and the problem of maximizing the constant term, and show that they are closely related to the Krzyż conjecture: the conjecture implies the analogous statement for all of them and, conversely, if one of them has the same extremal value as the Krzyż problem, then this value is $2/e$. This may represent a new approach to attacking the original problem. Finally, we show that for these problems an extremal function whose Taylor coefficients $a_1,\ldots,a_{\lfloor n/3\rfloor}$ vanish must be the conjectured one; as a special case, we obtain a new proof of a recent result of MacDonald.

papers.title: Enjoying the Product but Not Joining the Builders: Investigating Why Students Don't Contribute to OSS
papers.abstract: Open-source software (OSS) participation provides students with authentic exposure to collaborative, real-world software development, yet active contributions remain limited. This short paper presents an exploratory study of computing students' perceptions, knowledge, and experiences with OSS at the University of Hawai'i at Manoa. We administered a survey and analyzed 122 responses using both quantitative and qualitative methods. Students reported moderate OSS familiarity and frequent OSS use in coursework and personal projects, yet only 12.3% actively contributed and engagement with OSS communities was limited. Key barriers included skill gaps (72.89% of non-contributors), time constraints (59.81%), and codebase complexity (66.67% of contributors), often alongside imposter syndrome (36.45%). Students indicated that more time, mentorship, beginner-friendly issues, better onboarding/documentation, and curricular incentives (e.g., course credit) would most increase participation, while most reported their courses do not require or incentivize OSS contributions (58.20%). Grounded in a single institutional context, this study provides a nuanced understanding of how curriculum structure, faculty encouragement, and competing academic demands shape OSS participation. These insights inform the design of targeted curricular and institutional interventions aimed at supporting student onboarding and participation in OSS communities.

papers.title: Ori: Drift-Aware Streaming $k$-PCA for Very Low-Rank LLM Training
papers.abstract: A prominent family of low-rank LLM optimizers, pioneered by GaLore, performs gradient-subspace projection: at each step, they project the gradient into a low-dimensional subspace and map the update back to the full model. Most existing work either recomputes the gradient subspace at certain intervals, or performs post-hoc adaptation to catch up to the moving subspace. In this work, we explicitly identify in practice the slow, stable manner in which LLM gradient subspaces drift across time. To this end, we propose Ori, a novel low-rank optimizer for training LLMs that captures the shifting principal gradient directions over time to achieve state-of-the-art accuracy under stringent low-rank constraints. Ori employs a streaming $k$-PCA algorithm inspired by Oja++, whose low per-step cost enables high-frequency, on-the-fly subspace tracking. In practice, Ori reduces the performance gap of the state-of-the-art low-rank optimizers to full-rank optimizers by up to 69.3\% on a 1B LLaMA pretraining task, and achieves the best performance on 10 out of 16 task scenarios in Roberta-Base fine-tuning. Together, these contributions allow Ori to further push the performance and efficiency frontiers of gradient-projecting optimizers, narrowing the gap to full-rank training for LLMs. Code can be found at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/Ori-Submission-2132.

papers.title: Renormalisation of Hydrogen Partition Function and Saha Ionisation Equation
papers.abstract: An important physical quantity that is part of the Saha ionisation equation is the partition function of the neutral hydrogen atoms. An immense uncertainty is caused by the divergency of the neutral atom partition function arising due to the fast growing degeneracy factor of its excited n-state. We suggested a regularisation and renormalisation procedure for the partition function of the neutral hydrogen atoms. The renormalised partition function is well defined and allows to calculate the population of the energy levels and the ionisation state of the hydrogen plasma as a function of its temperature and pressure. In the low-temperature limit the behaviour of these functions smoothly transforms to the Saha equation, which is used in the description of the low-temperature plasma. At higher temperatures the renormalised ionisation equation describes the deviation from the Saha equation. The application of the renormalised ionisation equation to the solar core and atmosphere is considered.

papers.title: Embedding theorems for Herz-Type Sobolev spaces on domains
papers.abstract: In this paper, we further investigate the properties of Herz-type Sobolev spaces on domains, which unify and generalize the classical Sobolev spaces. In particular, we establish several Sobolev-type embedding theorems for these spaces. Moreover, by means of a suitable example, we show that some of the assumptions imposed on the parameters are optimal.

papers.title: Spectral asymmetry and odd cycles in integral graphs
papers.abstract: We prove that the triangle $C_3$ is the only integral unicyclic graph with an odd cycle. The main tool is a spectral inequality that does not require integrality: if $G$ is a connected non-bipartite graph and $G-e$ is bipartite for some edge $e$, then the eigenvalues $λ_1\ge\cdots\geλ_n$ of $G$ satisfy $\sum_{i}(λ_i+λ_{n+1-i})^+\le 2$ and $0<λ_1+λ_n\le 1$. It follows from comparing $A(G)$ with the signed adjacency matrix obtained by reversing the sign of $e$, which is similar to $-A(G)$, through a common rank-one perturbation and Weyl's monotonicity theorem. For integral graphs in this class, an arithmetic lemma then gives $λ_n=1-λ_1$ and at least $λ_1-1\ge1$ triangles, which yields the classification. We also prove that an integral graph of odd girth $g$ has at least $(g-1)!/2$ cycles of length $g$, with equality for the Petersen graph when $g=5$, and we derive consequences for quantum periodicity a

papers.title: Error analysis of a backward L2 method on graded meshes for linear and semilinear subdiffusion equations
papers.abstract: Time-fractional linear and semilinear parabolic equations with a Caputo time derivative of order $α\in(0,1)$ are considered. Their solutions exhibit an initial singularity of type $t^σ$ for any fixed $σ\in (0,1) \cup (1,2)$. A backward L2-type discrete fractional-derivative operator of order $3-α$ is considered on nonuniform temporal meshes. Sufficient conditions for inverse monotonicity of this operator areestablished. Hence, sharp pointwise-in-time error bounds are obtained on graded temporal meshes with arbitrary degree of grading. The theoretical findings are illustrated by numerical experiments.

papers.title: Clustering of JWST LRDs. Implications for PBHs and other early-forming seeds
papers.abstract: We use the observed abundance and spatial clustering of JWST little red dots (LRDs) over z = 4--8 to confront two formation scenarios: the standard picture in which LRDs form in virialized dark-matter halos, and one in which they are seeded by a dynamically subdominant population of primordial black holes (PBHs). The halo formation scenario accounts for both observables naturally and without fine-tuning. In the PBH scenario, matching the observed LRD abundance requires a negligibly small PBH mass fraction, and a power-spectrum analysis shows that such a Poisson isocurvature component predicts a clustering signal far below what is observed. The same conclusion holds for any population of dynamically subdominant early-forming seeds, unless their initial clustering is finely tuned or their activity is tied to massive host halos. We conclude that the spatial clustering of JWST LRDs strongly favours the standard halo formation picture and disfavours PBHs, or similar early-forming seeds, as a randomly activated LRD population; PBHs remain viable as seeds only if their activity is governed by massive host halos, in which case clustering alone cannot distinguish them from astrophysical seeds.

papers.intro:
The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) has opened a new observational window on the high-redshift Universe, revealing unexpectedly abundant and luminous galaxies at early cosmic times [1, 2, 3]. Although at least part of this initial tension can be alleviated through revisions to the modelling of galaxy formation and stellar populations [4], JWST has also uncovered populations whose very nature remains unsettled. Among the most enigmatic are the so-called little red dots (LRDs): compact sources found predominantly at z∼4z\sim 4–8, characterised by distinctive V-shaped rest-frame ultraviolet-to-optical spectral energy distributions and, in many cases, broad hydrogen emission lines [5, 6, 7, 8].

The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) has opened a new observational window on the high-redshift Universe, revealing unexpectedly abundant and luminous galaxies at early cosmic times [1, 2, 3]. Although at least part of this initial tension can be alleviated through revisions to the modelling of galaxy formation and stellar populations [4], JWST has also uncovered populations whose very nature remains unsettled. Among the most enigmatic are the so-called little red dots (LRDs): compact sources found predominantly at z∼4z\sim 4–8, characterised by distinctive V-shaped rest-frame ultraviolet-to-optical spectral energy distributions and, in many cases, broad hydrogen emission lines [5, 6, 7, 8].

Several interpretations of LRDs have been proposed, including heavily dust-obscured active galactic nuclei (AGN) [9], compact and extremely dense star-forming systems, and combinations of nuclear and stellar components [10, 11]. The extreme compactness of LRDs and their broad Balmer emission lines point towards accreting black holes, whereas weak X-ray [12] and mid-infrared [10, 11] emission and, in some sources, prominent Balmer breaks [6, 13] have motivated alternatives. Among the more exotic interpretations are supermassive stars, whose spectra can reproduce several of the observed ultraviolet-to-optical features without an AGN [14, 15, 16, 17] and which may form through runaway collisions in the extremely dense stellar cores implied by LRD compactness [18], and quasi-stars, in which a black hole accretes inside a radiation-pressure-supported gaseous envelope [19, 20, 21, 22, 23]. Recent spectroscopic observations and modelling, however, increasingly favour scenarios in which a substantial fraction of LRDs are powered by accreting black holes embedded in dense, optically thick gaseous envelopes—so-called black-hole stars—which can reproduce several characteristic spectral features [24, 25]. In this picture, the dense gas can account for the X-ray weakness and Balmer breaks of individual sources [26], while electron scattering can explain the broad line profiles [27]. The black-hole-star model is now being tested against detailed spectroscopy of individual sources [28, 29]. Related compact, ultraviolet-bright sources, the little blue dots, may be connected to LRDs, possibly representing similar systems viewed from different directions or in different accretion states [30, 31]. The inferred black-hole masses nevertheless remain uncertain: some analyses find black holes that are strongly overmassive relative to their hosts [32, 33], whereas others attribute the apparent overmassiveness to super-Eddington accretion, implying substantially lower black-hole masses [34, 35], of order 10410^{4}–105​M⊙10^{5}\,M_{\odot} for typical sources, consistent with seeds formed from single supermassive stars [35].

If accreting black holes power a substantial fraction of LRDs, a central question is how these black holes formed and reached their inferred masses by z∼4z\sim 4–8. Conventional scenarios invoke seeds from Population III stellar remnants or direct collapse, followed by efficient accretion [36, 37, 38, 39, 40, 41], with LRDs possibly marking the first accretion episodes of newly formed seeds [42]. A more exotic alternative is that some of these black holes originated as primordial black holes (PBHs). Enhanced small-scale primordial fluctuations could also shift the formation of the first stars to z≳100z\gtrsim 100; at z≳500z\gtrsim 500, where molecular-hydrogen formation is suppressed by the cosmic microwave background, supermassive stars of ∼105​M⊙\sim 10^{5}\,M_{\odot} could form through atomic cooling alone, providing another channel for very early-forming massive seeds [43]. Distinguishing between these possibilities is challenging, because the observed emission primarily probes the present accretion state rather than the formation mechanism of the underlying black hole.

If accreting black holes power a substantial fraction of LRDs, a central question is how these black holes formed and reached their inferred masses by z∼4z\sim 4–8. Conventional scenarios invoke seeds from Population III stellar remnants or direct collapse, followed by efficient accretion [36, 37, 38, 39, 40, 41], with LRDs possibly marking the first accretion episodes of newly formed seeds [42]. A more exotic alternative is that some of these black holes originated as primordial black holes (PBHs). Enhanced small-scale primordial fluctuations could also shift the formation of the first stars to z≳100z\gtrsim 100; at z≳500z\gtrsim 500, where molecular-hydrogen formation is suppressed by the cosmic microwave background, supermassive stars of ∼105​M⊙\sim 10^{5}\,M_{\odot} could form through atomic cooling alone, providing another channel for very early-forming massive seeds [43]. Distinguishing between these possibilities is challenging, because the observed emission primarily probes the present accretion state rather than the formation mechanism of the underlying black hole.

In this work we approach this question using two population-level observables: the comoving number density and the spatial clustering of LRDs [44]. Their abundance constrains the number of potential host halos or seeds, while their clustering carries information about the environments in which they reside; together they test whether a given formation scenario can consistently account for the observed population. We compare a conventional scenario, in which LRDs occupy virialized dark-matter halos, with one in which they are associated with a dynamically subdominant population of PBHs, and identify the conditions under which a PBH-seed interpretation could remain viable. Since the PBH argument relies only on the seeds being early-forming and dynamically subdominant, our conclusions apply more broadly to any such seed population.

papers.title: Jarvis: Coordination Deserves a Brain of Its Own in Agentic Interactive Models
papers.abstract: Interactive models increasingly hand complex reasoning and tool use to a slow brain in the background, leaving a realtime front model free to sustain full-duplex dialogue. Yet the user may refine, cancel or replace a request while its task runs, so a plan or result that made sense a moment ago goes stale. Each new utterance must therefore be read against the work in flight, but the front model follows only the conversation and the back end sees only its own task. Coordination deserves a brain of its own, one that sees both. We introduce Jarvis, a coordination harness where models judge and code enforces. Its typed decision model, JEV, reads each turn against the live tasks and picks among operations built from a versioned task record. Code checks every choice against the current state before applying it, so no decision can act on a task version the user has replaced. Jarvis also rechecks plans before they execute and results before they are spoken, and counts an answer as delivered only once the user has heard it in full. We build two instances of this design. Jarvis-Audio runs unchanged on three full-duplex speech models. Jarvis-Omni adds vision and rechecks the evidence behind an answer before and during playback, since a scene can change while nobody speaks. With the front model and back end held fixed, replacing Qwen Audio Agent with Jarvis raises tau-Voice task success more than sixfold, from 29 to 192 of 278 tasks, and the gains hold on every benchmark and front model. Against published systems, Jarvis-Audio reaches 69% Pass1 on Full-Duplex-Bench v3 with an open 9B front model, versus 60% for GPT-Realtime. These results suggest that how the two brains are coordinated matters as much as how strong they are.

papers.title: The semiring of spectral duality skeletons: cancellation, characters and factorization
papers.abstract: Weighted dual skeletons are the combinatorial core of spectral duality structures. Their isomorphism classes, under Cartesian product and disjoint union, form a semiring graded by the degree. We identify it completely: a class is determined by its degree, a symmetric element of the group semiring N_0[R] and its number of fixed points. Equivalently, skeletons of a given degree are finite C_2-sets over the C_2-monoid (R,+), these data are their marks, and the semiring is an infinite-monoid analogue of a crossed Burnside semiring. The multiplicative monoid is not cancellative, the only obstruction being that multiplication by a skeleton without fixed points forgets the fixed points; accordingly, the Grothendieck ring has explicit zero divisors. A continuous family of semiring characters, with the degree and the number of fixed points, is a complete invariant, and for commensurable ratios the multiplicative Grothendieck group is described by Pólya's theorem. The main subject is factorization. The reduced monoid is atomic with bounded lengths, but factorization is not unique, the elasticity is infinite, and even the divisor-closed submonoid with one fixed point is not half-factorial. Without fixed points, every reducible skeleton splits off a single orbit, which gives a criterion by centers, exactly when the number of orbits is 8, 16, a prime or twice a prime. Irreducibility is generic in almost every type. Progression skeletons factor according to mixed-radix number systems, with all factorizations of equal length. Finally, orbit counting gives the dimension of the separatrix and the response rank of products.

papers.title: VesperCSI: A High-Performance and Extensible CSI Acquisition Framework for Edge Wi-Fi Sensing
papers.abstract: Channel State Information (CSI) captures fine-grained changes in Wi-Fi channel propagation and provides a foundation for device-free sensing applications such as activity recognition, localization, and occupancy detection. The development of such applications depends on an acquisition system that can handle high-rate CSI streams while remaining extensible to the requirements of individual experiments. VesperCSI is an open-source, GPL-3.0-licensed redesign of FeitCSI for CSI acquisition with Intel AX200 and AX210 Wi-Fi interfaces. It targets high-rate acquisition on amd64 and aarch64 Linux hosts using fixed-capacity preallocated object pools and separate capture and consumer threads. A loadable plugin interface supports experiment-specific monitoring, storage, and processing. We evaluate VesperCSI and FeitCSI on Raspberry Pi CM4 receivers in a burst-traffic software crossover. At a 600-MHz all-core frequency ceiling and a target rate of 2500 frames/s, VesperCSI achieves mean sequence retention of 99.017-99.087% in 10,000-frame bursts, compared with 43.972-46.553% for FeitCSI. This ordering persists after exchanging the userspace programs between two receivers while retaining their respective drivers. The comparison therefore characterizes the tested software-and-driver packages rather than isolating userspace effects. These results support VesperCSI as a reusable acquisition component for edge-hosted Wi-Fi sensing under the evaluated workload and platform conditions.

papers.title: Ultra-stable laser with sub-Hz intrinsic linewidth using a silicon photonic chip
papers.abstract: Here, we demonstrate a novel optical self-injection-locking scheme integrated with a modulation-free laser frequency stabilization technique co-integrated with a compact vacuum-gap micro-Fabry-Perot cavity (uFP), with Q-factor of 3.46E9, to realize an ultra-stable laser with sub-Hz fundamental linewidth using a silicon photonic chip. The demonstrated electro-optic self-injection locking (EOSIL) chip suppresses a commercial DFB diode laser's frequency noise power spectral density by more than 110 dB at 1 Hz offset, approaching the theoretical thermal noise limit of the uFP cavity, and enables a laser fundamental linewidth of 58 mHz with a fractional frequency instability of 8.68E-13 at 1 sec averaging time. The chip is fabricated using the Advanced Micro Foundry standard silicon photonic process and occupies a footprint of 10 mm^2.

papers.title: Area Theorems for Quantum Error Correction
papers.abstract: The extrinsic information transfer (EXIT) and generalized EXIT (GEXIT) area theorems provide fundamental conservation laws that connect the rate of classical codes to the performance of maximum-a-posteriori decoding on binary memoryless channels. In this work, we generalize these area theorems to quantum error correction. We first develop a coset-entropy formalism for nested linear codes, where the message specifies a coset and encoder randomization selects a codeword within that coset. The area under the resulting coset (G)EXIT function equals the normalized dimension of the quotient. For stabilizer codes, the measured syndrome restricts the Pauli error but does not always determine its logical effect, and the remaining uncertainty is an entropy over logical correction classes. We show that this entropy equals a classical coset entropy associated with the stabilizer group and the Pauli operators that commute with it. The resulting quantum GEXIT function has area equal to the number of encoded qubits per channel use for any stabilizer code, and this applies to the depolarizing channel through its joint four-valued Pauli-error distribution. For CSS codes on the quantum erasure channel and under independent bit- and phase-flip noise, the logical correction problem separates into two binary coset-decoding problems. On the quantum erasure channel, the duality between the stabilizer group and the Pauli operators that commute with it gives a folding identity at complementary erasure probabilities. Using this and the area theorem, we derive an upper bound on the rate of code families with vanishing logical error probability that matches the capacity of the quantum erasure channel. For the depolarizing channel, we also derive a rate-dependent converse, using a connection between correction-class entropy and coherent information to establish an inequality involving the complementary channel.

papers.title: Trajectory-Triggered Sparse Collaborative Decoding
papers.abstract: Dense assistance methods such as speculative decoding repeatedly verify draft tokens with a target model, keeping target computation coupled to generation. We study sparse collaborative decoding, where a draft model generates most tokens and a target model is invoked only for short corrective segments. The key problem is deciding when to call the target. We show that local uncertainty is a weak trigger: entropy, negative log-likelihood, logit margin, top-$k$ mass, and velocity features give near-chance failure prediction, with AUC 0.50-0.53. In contrast, aggregate trajectory-shape features over the draft confidence path reach AUC 0.86 using a lightweight logistic predictor trained only from draft correctness labels. This induces a trigger-timing tradeoff: early calls have more leverage but weaker evidence, while later calls have stronger evidence but less ability to redirect the trajectory. Used online, learned sparse collaborative decoding improves over the best open-loop schedule by +5.3 to +20.0 accuracy points across five GSM8K draft-target pairs. On MATH-500, it gains 7.0-13.5 points when early prediction and target competence align, but loses when either is weak. On StrategyQA, it improves over open-loop by 5.0-8.3 points, showing transfer beyond arithmetics.

authors.name: Steven Li
authors.institution: VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland

papers.title: Stereo LWIR-RGB Automatic Labeling for Low-Light Camera-Based VRU Detection
papers.abstract: VRU detection in low-light conditions is a key component in ensuring VRU safety during the most collision prone time of the day. Currently, advances in low-light detection are limited due to the lack of large scale datasets and automated labeling methods. Most autolabeling methods use RGB detections as their labels source, which cannot be replicated in low-light conditions. To fill this gap in this paper we present an automated pipeline for low-light VRU labeling. We use LWIR-RGB image pairs and source our labels from LWIR as VRUs differentiate from the background due to their body temperature. Unlike our previous work that relied on a complex hardware setup to align the two modalities, we perform this experiment using a LWIR-RGB stereo setup, lowering hardware complexity and cost, making the pipeline easier to reproduce. We evaluate method end-to-end on a dataset collected in the capital region of Finland. Models trained on our generated labels beat both off-the-shelf baselines and models fine tuned on a hand labeled subset on F1, mAP@50 and LAMR metrics when tested on a manually labeled dataset, and the result holds for two different LWIR detectors. This shows that low-light VRU autolabeling can be made both accessible and effective without specialized alignment hardware.

papers.title: Designing Human-AI Collaborative Science: The 9A Framework
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) for Science is often described as a progression from human-directed assistance toward increasingly autonomous AI scientists. Human-AI collaboration offers a further mode in which human and AI contributions substantively shape scientific reasoning, judgments, and the course of inquiry. Existing research addresses work allocation, human-AI coordination, and system evaluation, but how these aspects interact to shape collaborative scientific systems remains insufficiently articulated. We develop the 9A Framework for Human-AI Collaborative Science (HACS) to connect these considerations across three layers. The organization layer specifies what scientific activities are required (Activity), who performs them (Actor), and who holds authority over consequential decisions (Authority). The coordination layer addresses how participants access relevant research information (Awareness), how scientific work advances through iterative proposal, execution, examination, revision, and resolution (Accountability), and when collaborative arrangements should be adjusted (Adaptability). The evaluation layer establishes what constitutes effective system performance (Achievement), how comparisons can be designed to identify the effects of organizational and coordination choices (Attribution), and what evidence supports the resulting conclusions (Assurance). Together, these layers frame HACS as a system-design problem, providing a basis for designing collaborative scientific workflows and for empirically comparing their effectiveness.

papers.title: Water-Energy-Data nexus reveals sustainability gaps and priorities for AI infrastructure
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) depends on interconnected water, energy, and data systems spanning infrastructure life cycles and diverse geographies, with the potential to intensify water and energy insecurity, exacerbate social inequities and lead to cascading sustainability issues globally. Yet assessments commonly examine them separately, limiting our understanding of where resource pressures arise, how they are transferred across space, and who bears their consequences. To address these challenges, we established a water-energy-data (WED) nexus framework that captures the spatial and life-cycle dependencies of AI infrastructure, and use large language models to synthesize 12,825 water- or energy-related studies across four resource-intensive AI infrastructure activities: mineral extraction, semiconductor manufacturing, data center operation and electronic-waste processing. The evidence map identifies a mismatch between the interconnected activities supporting AI infrastructure and boundaries used to assess them. Researchers assess operational energy more than water use and other indirect demands, while interactions across locations and life-cycle activities remain understudied. These gaps obscure how resource demands shift among infrastructure nodes and regions, and how data-enabled benefits compare with their underlying costs. The WED nexus provides a foundation for integrated assessment of spatially metacoupled systems, while the evidence map can inform priorities for managing the sustainability implications of the AI boom.

authors.name: Jincheng Huang
authors.institution: Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Two Seconds per Day: Limitations of Circadian Burden Metrics in the Permanent Daylight Saving Time Debate
papers.abstract: A 1410-word Letter to the Editor reporting a bug in a study published in PNAS. The authors of the original study executed their code to compute the yearly circadian burden with an Earth rotating backwards: the sun rising in the West, setting on the East. The authors have acknowledged the error and re-executed the code. We analyze authors's new average yearly circadian burden in the US to show that these results do not provide significant information for the current debate on the time policy.

papers.title: Uncertainty-aware AI-enabled framework for predicting hydrogen dispersion in confined spaces to enhance operator situational awareness
papers.abstract: We present a two-stage AI-enabled framework for enhancing operator situational awareness during compressed hydrogen bunkering in maritime confined spaces. In the event of a leak, the framework first estimates the unknown leakage rate from early sensor readings and then forecasts how the hydrogen cloud will disperse over the next time steps, providing operators with a predicted concentration map together with confidence bounds. The framework is based on two independent AI models building one AI system. The AI system is designed as a decision-support tool. It augments sensor readings, and thus enhances operator situational awareness and supports decision-making. This enables preventive safety barriers to be deployed before hazardous concentrations are reached, while an independent emergency shutdown system remains the ultimate safety layer. The system design incorporates safeguards to ensure the AI system operates within its competence envelope. Trained and tested on an open dataset of confined-space hydrogen releases, the framework achieves a mean absolute error of $0.052$~g/s in leakage-rate estimation and $\approx0.018$ in hydrogen-concentration prediction, approaching the sensor precision bound of $\pm0.01$. The hydrogen-concentration prediction provides well-calibrated uncertainty estimates that allow operators to judge the reliability of each forecast. These results suggest that the framework may provide early information about hazardous concentration build-up, potentially supporting preventive actions by operators.

papers.title: Derivations and quasi-derivations of Block Lie superalgebras $S(q)$
papers.abstract:
We compute the homogeneous derivations and the homogeneous quasi-derivations of the Block Lie superalgebras $S(q)$, whose even part is the Block Lie algebra $\mathcal{B}(q)$. For every $q\in\mathbb C$, the space $\mathfrak{Der}_θ(S(q))$ is the direct sum of the inner derivations and an explicitly given finite-dimensional space of outer derivations; in particular, for $q
eq0$ a new odd outer derivation appears if and only if $q\in2\mathbb Z^*$. For $q\in\mathbb C^*$ we prove that $\mathfrak{QDer}(S(q))=\mathfrak{Der}(S(q))\oplus\langle \idangle$ if $q
otin\mathbb Z$, and that for $q\in\mathbb Z^{*}$ the superalgebra $S(q)$ has an infinite-dimensional space of nontrivial quasi-derivations, namely all graded linear maps with values in the center. For $q=0$ we also describe all homogeneous quasi-derivations: modulo maps with values in the center, they are spanned by $\id$, three further maps and infinite families of maps shifting the $\mathbb Z^2$-grading; in particular, $\mathfrak{QDer}(S(0))/\mathfrak{Der}(S(0))$ is infinite-dimensional. As corollaries, we obtain the complete description of homogeneous $δ$-derivations of $S(q)$, $q
eq0$, and prove that, in contrast with the Block Lie algebras $\mathcal{B}(q)$, the superalgebras $S(q)$, $q
eq0$, do not admit nontrivial transposed $δ$-Poisson superalgebra structures for any $δ
otin\{0,1\}$.

papers.title: The algebraic and geometric classification of semi-alternative superalgebras
papers.abstract: The algebraic and geometric classifications of complex $3$-dimensional semi-alternative superalgebras are given. As corollaries, we obtain the algebraic and geometric classifications of complex $3$-dimensional $\mathfrak{perm}$, associative, and assosymmetric superalgebras.

papers.title: Quasi-derivations of the (extended) Schrödinger--Witt algebras
papers.abstract: The Schrödinger--Witt algebras are infinite-dimensional Lie algebras of local dynamical symmetries of the free Schrödinger equation; they contain the Witt algebra of conformal transformations of the time line and appear in non-equilibrium statistical physics and in non-relativistic conformal field theory. We describe all quasi-derivations of the original and the twisted Schrödinger--Witt algebras. We prove that every quasi-derivation is the sum of a derivation, a trivial $\frac12$-derivation, a linear map with values in the center, and a finite linear combination of maps from three new families of quasi-derivations. As corollaries, we describe all $δ$-derivations, all $δ$-biderivations and all transposed $δ$-Poisson structures of the Schrödinger--Witt algebras. Finally, we prove that every quasi-derivation of the (original or twisted) extended Schrödinger--Witt algebra is the sum of an inner derivation and a multiple of the identity map. As a consequence, there are no nontrivial $δ$-derivations (for $δ\notin \{\frac12,1\}$), $δ$-biderivations (for $δ\neq1$), and transposed $δ$-Poisson structures on these algebras.

authors.institution: Academy of Sciences Republic of Uzbekistan

papers.title: Fully relativistic calculation of thermal shifts in spectra of hydrogen molecular ion
papers.abstract: Within a fully relativistic framework, we discuss the one-loop self-energy correction, generalized to the presence of external blackbody radiation, for a bound electron in the hydrogen molecular ion. The calculations rely on the thermal part of the photon propagator from finite-temperature quantum electrodynamics. The ADKB method, which extends the dual kinetic balance condition to axially symmetric systems, is adopted together with a B-spline-based trial function. The results are obtained within the Born-Oppenheimer adiabatic approximation. Thermal shift for the ground term of the hydrogen molecular ion is computed as a function of the internuclear distance. Including this correction, we present the resulting shifts of the vibrational levels. The analysis focuses on the dynamical effect, a comparison is made with data available in the current literature.

authors.name: M. A. Reiter
authors.institution: New Mexico Institute of Mining and Technology

papers.title: Field-induced incommensurate--commensurate transitions in anisotropic magnets
papers.abstract: We study field-induced incommensurate--commensurate transitions (ICTs) in classical spin chains with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI) $D$, strong easy-plane anisotropy, and weak easy-axis anisotropy $A$ within the easy plane. This model describes systems with ferromagnetic layers coupled by exchange interaction with DMI. The magnetic field $\bf H$ is applied in the easy plane at an arbitrary angle $δ$ to the easy axis stabilizing a soliton lattice in the ground state. We consider ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic in-chain exchange interactions within the continuum limit and show that the easy-axis anisotropy leads to qualitatively different effects in these two cases: the ferromagnetic chain is described by a double-sine-Gordon-type equation with phase-shifted harmonics, whereas the antiferromagnetic chain reduces to a sine-Gordon equation. For the latter case, phase boundaries between incommensurate and commensurate states are found analytically in $(H,A,D,δ)$ space and confirmed by numerical calculations for certain $D$ and $δ$ values. Close to all ICTs, results of the continuum consideration become invalid due to a stochastic destruction of near-separatrix solutions which either make an ICT a first-order transition or stabilize states with spatially irregular soliton and antisoliton arrangements.

papers.title: Broadband chiroptical sensing with two-mode subwavelength grating waveguides
papers.abstract: Engineering local optical chirality in planar photonic structures offers a route to selective and enhanced light-matter interactions with chiral media. Here, we introduce periodic dielectric waveguides that support chiral evanescent fields through the interaction of two nearly degenerate waveguide modes. We develop a perturbation theory for such a waveguide covered by a chiral layer, relating chirality-induced modal coupling and propagation-constant corrections to measurable intermodal power conversion and differential transmission. Whereas modal detuning confines the chiral response of a symmetric waveguide to a narrow spectral range, mode hybridization in an asymmetric waveguide creates individual eigenmodes that carry nonzero local chirality over a broad spectral range. We show that modal dichroism in realistic lossy waveguides can produce a significant background differential transmission signal. Such a background, however, can be suppressed by comparing transmission through two asymmetric waveguides with opposite structural asymmetries, allowing the chiral response to be reliably extracted. Together, these findings provide a basis for developing integrated photonic components with locally chiral fields, including waveguides, metasurfaces, and resonators.

papers.title: Integrated sensing, communications, and identification for low-altitude economy
papers.abstract: With the rapid development of low-altitude economy (LAE), low-altitude information networks (LAINs) must provide reliable communication, environmental sensing, and target identification to support efficient and safe airspace operation. Although integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) provides a foundation for the joint design of communication and sensing, identification must also be incorporated to meet airspace safety and regulatory requirements. This paper reviews integrated sensing, communications, and identification (ISCAI) for LAE. We first review low-altitude communication, sensing, and identification approaches and explain how representative applications motivate their integration. We then summarize low-altitude ISAC fundamentals, including system architectures, channel modeling, unified signal models, and performance metrics, followed by communication-centric and sensing-centric designs, resource allocation, and aircraft trajectory optimization. Building on these, we introduce ISCAI, focusing on a backscatter communication (BackCom)-based identification mechanism in which backscatter devices serve as electronic license plates for aircraft. We present system and signal models for integrated sensing and identification (ISAI) and ISCAI, together with multifunctional receiver designs and mutual integration gains. Finally, we discuss open problems and future directions, including an information-theoretic framework, artificial intelligence-empowered system design, and reconfigurable intelligent surface-enhanced ISCAI. This review provides a structured perspective on the evolution of LAINs toward integrated communication, sensing, and identification.

authors.name: Shanxing Zeng
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Jun Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Peak-Memory Schedules You Can Trust: Exact Realization, Certified Optimality, and the Limits of Recomputation for Inference
papers.abstract: Real-time inference on small devices needs low activation memory without extra latency, which makes operator order the most valuable memory lever: it is free in time. We show that the usual way of deploying a better order, handing it back to the compiler and regenerating code, is unreliable. In PyTorch Inductor the regenerated program misses its predicted peak in 22 of 54 CPU configurations. It is worse than the stock program in 9 of them and in 19 of 50 on a GPU, and on the GPU it also changes numerical results. We instead profile the generated program, model its memory exactly from its own statements and their read/write effects, and permute those statements. We prove that this realizes the modeled peak whenever allocation does not depend on history. It does so to the byte, with bitwise-identical results, in all our CPU runs. On the GPU we characterize why the caching allocator breaks the condition. To know when to stop, we give forward and reverse "trap" lower bounds, each computable with $O(n^2)$ minimum cuts. They certify the found order optimal for 94% of held-out wrapper graphs and all 16 microcontroller-class models we study, in under a second. So most inference graphs are already scheduled optimally. Branching networks are the exception, where reordering is free and pays, e.g. 10.0% on DeepLabV3. In compiled training we save up to 7.6%. Beyond the certified optimum we study selective recomputation with per-operator caps. It is strongly NP-hard for every fixed cap even at treewidth two, encodes knapsack exactly on series-parallel graphs, and is solvable exactly on bounded treewidth. It is useless on public tiny models whose peak is a single layer, but on architectures that hold a cheap value for a late reuse it pays: on the public ReDimNet speaker networks, whose order is already optimal, it lowers the peak by 5.2-6.1% at under 0.4% extra MACs, with bitwise-identical outputs.

authors.name: Ivan Fomin
authors.institution: H.S. Skovoroda Kharkiv National Pedagogical University

papers.title: Data Provenance Aggregation and Structural Descriptors for Query-Template Identification
papers.abstract: Runtime query similarity identification supports several activities, including workload analysis, identifying recurring behaviour, auditing, debugging, and anomaly detection. Existing methods for evaluating query similarity mostly rely on SQL text, execution plans, or result values but do not account for input data or how results are derived during query execution. This paper proposes a novel approach using data provenance for query-template identification. We construct query-level profiles that capture explicit data dependencies, occurrence frequencies, and structural properties by aggregating tuple-level Lineage and Why-provenance across entire query results. We also derive Provenance Structural Descriptors (PSD), which summarise these profiles using a small set of numerical features. We evaluate our proposals using these profiles to identify query templates over \(12{,}500\) distinct query instances generated from parametrised TPC-DS query templates. The experimental evaluation shows that query templates can be identified solely from their provenance footprints, and that accuracy improves as more historical data becomes available. It also shows that PSD achieve high classification accuracy with limited training history and low test-processing cost.

authors.name: José Moreira
authors.institution: Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul

papers.title: Earth Observation Satellite Scheduling Models: Taxonomy, Classification and Open Challenges
papers.abstract: Over the past three decades, a large number of optimization models have been proposed for Earth observation satellite (EOS) scheduling. The main goal of this paper is to provide an overview of these models and to relate them to the characteristics of the problems they address. To do so, we first identify the main features of EOS scheduling problems and those with the most impact on the computational complexity of the model. Based on these features, we propose a new taxonomy of satellite agility and a classification of EOS scheduling problems that allows the problem under study to be clearly identified. We then propose a classification of the optimization models into five categories, based on their time and event representations, and describe representative formulations of each category in a unified notation, together with their extensions, discussing the respective advantages and limitations. The trade-offs between the alternative representations are analyzed, showing that discrete-time formulations allow time-dependent parameters, such as transition times and image quality, to be pre-computed, which preserves the linearity of the model but makes its size depend on the adopted discretization, whereas continuous-time formulations treat these parameters as functions of the start times, which introduces nonlinearities unless simplifying assumptions are adopted. Finally, we identify the main open challenges, including the exact modeling of time-dependent transition times and the integrated scheduling of active imaging satellites.

papers.title: A Class of Rényi-based Concentration Metrics for Kolmogorov-Arnold Geometry in Multilayer Perceptrons
papers.abstract: The interpretability of artificial intelligence models has become a central concern, especially for black-box models such as multilayer perceptrons (MLPs). Kolmogorov-Arnold Geometry has recently emerged as a framework for analysing the internal representations of these networks, by examining how the hidden layer locally responds to changes in the input through the minors of its Jacobian. The degree to which a few of these minors dominate the rest, known as their concentration, has so far been measured with the Participation Ratio. Although this metric has useful properties, its maximum value depends on the size of the network, so a given value cannot be read as high or low concentration without reference to the architecture. To overcome this limitation, in this paper we propose the $α$-RC metrics, a family of Rényi-based concentration measures that compare the normalized magnitudes of the minors with the uniform distribution through the Rényi divergence of order $α$. All the metrics in the family are bounded between 0 and 1 regardless of the architecture, with 0 indicating that the magnitude is evenly spread over the minors and 1 that it is carried by a single one. Moreover, the metrics are non-decreasing in $α$, and for $α$ = 2 they reduce to an explicit transformation of the Participation Ratio. Computational experiments with single-hidden-layer MLPs trained on a synthetic dataset show the benefits of our proposal.

papers.title: Memory effects in the homogenization of a viscous fluid containing small elastic particles
papers.abstract: This work deals with a fluid-structure interaction problem involving an incompressible viscous fluid and a periodic array of tiny elastic inclusions in a three-dimensional domain. We focus on a critical regime where the volume fraction of the inclusions tends to zero, but their density and stiffness are scaled so that they still influence the macroscopic behavior. The asymptotic regime depends on the parameter $γ=\lim_{\varepsilon\to 0}r_\varepsilon/\varepsilon^3\in [0,+\infty]$, where $\varepsilon$ is the period and $r_\varepsilon$ the inclusion size. For $γ=0$ the solid and fluid equations uncouple in the limit. For $γ\in (0,+\infty]$, we show that the macroscopic fluid velocity satisfies a Stokes system with memory: the standard Stokes equations are augmented by convolution-in-time terms arising from the elastic vibrations of the inclusions. The existence of the convolution kernels is established for both $γ\in(0,+\infty)$ and $γ=\infty$ using semigroup theory. For $γ=\infty$ the microscopic problem reduces to a purely conservative elastodynamic equation and the kernels can be computed explicitly via spectral decomposition. They are oscillatory and almost-periodic in time, yielding a persistent, non-decaying memory. For $γ\in(0,+\infty)$ the microscopic elastodynamic equation is coupled to a local Stokes problem, whose viscous dissipation yields memory kernels that decay to zero at infinity.

papers.title: A stable multipersistence invariant for ladder modules
papers.abstract: We define an additive functor S that assigns a three parameter persistence module to every morphism between one parameter persistence modules. We show that if the morphism is bar-to-bar, then its image under S is rectangle decomposable. We prove that S is stable with respect to the interleaving distance and study further properties of the functor related to rectangle decompositions.

papers.title: An Efficient Blind Detection of OFDM Signals with Unknown Parameters
papers.abstract: This study investigates efficient detector designs for the blind detection of orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) signals with unknown power, bandwidth, and carrier frequency in wideband spectrum sensing. We first describe the received signal model and conduct an asymptotic covariance analysis to obtain a tractable discrete-time representation. Based on this model, generalized likelihood ratio test (GLRT) detectors are derived for both known and unknown noise power cases in a single-antenna receiver setting. The proposed framework is subsequently extended to multi-antenna receivers, and the corresponding multi-antenna GLRT detectors are developed for both known and unknown noise power cases. Importantly, using the cumulative-sum (CUSUM) operations, the resulting detectors reduce to an efficient one-dimensional (1D) search in both single-antenna and multi-antenna settings. We also provide theoretical analysis for the conventional energy detector (Conv-ED) and the hypothetical uniformly most powerful (UMP) test to reveal the impact of system parameters on detection performance. In addition, computational complexity analysis is presented for both the proposed and conventional detectors. Finally, comprehensive simulation results are provided to evaluate the probability of detection. The results demonstrate that the proposed detectors achieve performance close to that of a genie-aided detector while significantly outperforming conventional detection approaches.

papers.title: Homology and carrier faces of simplicial distributions
papers.abstract: We study the facial structure of simplicial distribution polytopes using topological and algebraic methods. In the theory of simplicial distributions, measurement and event spaces are represented by simplicial sets, and compatible probability assignments form a convex polytope. Given a simplicial distribution, it is known that its supports determine its carrier face. Moreover, the supports form a simplicial subset of the event space. This naturally raises the question of how the topology of this simplicial subset is related to the corresponding carrier face. Our main objective is to relate the dimension of the carrier face to the topology and combinatorial structure of the space of supports. For $n$-facet-paired measurement spaces, we first express the carrier dimension in terms of the nullity of an associated facet matrix. When the measurement space is additionally orientable, we show that the carrier dimension is determined by the top-dimensional homology of the space of supports, yielding, in particular, a homological criterion for detecting vertices. We then develop an algebraic reduction based on a strong connectivity relation on the generating simplices of the space of supports. This construction yields a reduced facet matrix, indexed by the strongly connected components, whose null space is isomorphic to that of the original facet matrix. As a consequence, both the carrier dimension and extremality can be determined from the topology of the support and the way its strongly connected components are glued together.

papers.title: Active Learning for Interatomic Potentials: A Review of Uncertainty-Driven Data Efficiency
papers.abstract: Developing a machine learning interatomic potential (MLIP) that is accurate for the specific conditions under which it will be applied, rather than simply for the predefined configurations chosen by the model developer, is a significant challenge in atomistic simulation. Active learning (AL) addresses this challenge by closing the loop between candidate generation, data selection, reference calculation, and model updating. Here, we survey more than seventy studies, with an emphasis on work from 2020 to 2026, to understand how active learning has evolved from a niche, on-the-fly training technique for query-by-committee and Gaussian process force fields into a diverse family of data-efficient strategies. he reviewed examples include on-the-fly molecular dynamics, active data selection for fine-tuning pretrained models, kernel- and representation-based acquisition using frozen pretrained models, and reaction-aware sampling for chemical systems far from equilibrium. We explore the use of active learning in elemental and alloy mechanics, hydrogen and ion diffusion, ferroelectrics and effective Hamiltonians of functional materials, reactive and photochemical dynamics, high-entropy and compositionally disordered materials, as well as generative and autonomous material discovery pipelines. Drawing on a growing body of critical, methodologically self-aware literature, we also show that this achievement carries systematic caveats. Uncertainty estimates are not interchangeable across model architectures and are frequently the least reliable exactly where they matter most. We close by discussing the outlook for standardized, uncertainty-calibrated, and observable-targeted active-learning workflows in the foundation-model era.

authors.institution: Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Bridging Compressed Communication and Local Steps via Spectral Method in Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative training of complex models across large-scale networks of edge devices while keeping data localized. However, data heterogeneity and high communication overhead remain fundamental bottlenecks. Recently, the spectral optimizer Muon has demonstrated remarkable advantages over Adam-like methods in centralized training. While recent efforts have attempted to transition Muon to FL, naive integrations into traditional architectures fail short. Crucially, existing approaches do not support the the communication compression and local steps --- the two foundational techniques of efficient FL. To address this limitation, we introduce a novel spectral FL method that utilizes both local updates and compression. We establish rigorous convergence guarantees under mild assumptions, notably eliminating the restrictive bounded heterogeneity condition. Empirical evaluation on standard image classification benchmarks validates the efficiency and robustness of our approach.

authors.name: Dmitriy Bystrov
authors.institution: Tashkent State Technical University named after Islam Karimov

authors.name: Aleksandr Beznosikov
authors.institution: Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology

papers.title: Anytime Contracts for AI Services
papers.abstract: AI services are prone to moral hazard, as model providers can silently route requests to cheaper, lower-quality models, and the inherent stochasticity of model outputs makes this degradation hard to detect. Contract theory addresses moral hazard by designing payment rules that reward high-quality outputs and prevent strategic overcharging. However, existing frameworks assume interactions of fixed duration, whereas AI services are typically consumed through subscriptions and pay-as-you-go APIs that users can terminate at any time based on observed performance. We show that this flexibility can break standard contracts, opening them up to abuse by either the providers or users. To address this, we extend contract theory to account for unknown exit rules. We formalize the problem as a Principal-Agent game, and show that budget-optimal contracts in this setting are proportional to anytime-valid hypothesis tests based on likelihood-ratio e-values. We give an efficient algorithm for computing anytime contracts and show how betting e-processes can be used to approximate them when the models are unknown. Finally, we evaluate our findings on synthetic data and data from deployed LLMs.

papers.title: Hemicompactness and the $k_ω$-property of free topological vector spaces
papers.abstract: For a Tychonoff space $X$ we consider the vector space $E(X)$ with basis $X$ endowed with one of the following topologies: the weak topologies $L_b(X)$ and $L_p(X)$ generated by $C_b(X)$ and $C(X)$, the free locally convex space $L(X)$, the free locally $r$-convex space $L^{(r)}(X)$ ($0<r\le1$), the free locally pseudoconvex space $L^{(0)}(X)$, and the free topological vector space $V(X)$. We prove that $L_b(X)$ is hemicompact if and only if $X$ is finite; that for every vector topology between $L_p(X)$ and $L^{(0)}(X)$ hemicompactness is equivalent to $X$ being countable with all compact subsets finite; and that $V(X)$, as well as the free topological groups $F(X)$ and $A(X)$, are hemicompact if and only if $X$ is hemicompact. In particular, $V([0,1])$ is hemicompact, while $L([0,1])$ and $L_p([0,1])$ are not. We also describe when these spaces are $k_ω$-spaces: $L_b(X)$ and $L_p(X)$ only for finite $X$, and $L^{(r)}(X)$, $0\le r\le1$, only for countable discrete $X$.

papers.title: A new submillimeter Class I methanol maser at 345.903 GHz near the massive protostar S255IR NIRS3
papers.abstract: We present results of further investigation of radio emission from the remarkable molecular core S255IR-SMA1 harboring a \(\sim\) 20 Msun young stellar object NIRS3 which exhibited a disk-mediated accretion burst in 2015. Our study is based on observations of this object with ALMA in Band 7 with the longest baselines, which provide an angular resolution of \(\sim\)15 mas. The obtained data reveal several spots in the bright and narrow methanol 16(1) \(-\) 15(2) A\(-\) line emission at 345.903 GHz. These spots are located close to H_2O masers, knots in the jet and arc-like structures seen in submillimeter continuum. At the same time, they are far away from the peaks of the Class II methanol maser spots. High brightness temperatures and small line widths of the 345.903 GHz line emission indicate that this emission has a maser nature. Association with the shock tracers tells that these masers belong to Class I methanol maser category. Non-LTE analysis of the physical parameters which lead to population inversion of 16(1) \(-\) 15(2) A\(-\) transition shows that some known rare Class I methanol maser transitions are also inverted under these conditions.

papers.title: Reverse Urysohn inequality for functions and functional Shephard problem
papers.abstract: The results obtained in this paper provide a generalization of some geometric inequalities to the class of log-concave functions. They describe the relationships between the Quermassintegrals of functions and bodies, giving estimates for constants involved in functional Shephard-type problems.

papers.title: SIT-Eval: Situation-Based Interactive Turn-by-Turn Evaluation of Conversational Agents
papers.abstract: The rapid proliferation of conversational AI agents necessitates evaluation methods that assess performance across diverse dialogue scenarios, utilizing multiple situational criteria, as appropriate behavior depends on context and encompasses various aspects. Existing dialogue benchmarks typically use static natural conversations, which underrepresent rare situations---a critical safety gap, as low-probability events become frequent failures at production scale. However, limited sample sizes force a choice: either maintain natural dialogues for realism or turn to adaptive situation sampling for comprehensive yet statistically reliable coverage. We introduce SIT-Eval, an adjustable framework for evaluating situation-based conversational agents. We formalize an agent's desired behavior as situational rules: if situation is P, follow rules Q. At each conversation turn, an LLM-interlocutor enacts a uniformly sampled situation. A context-aware LLM-judge leverages all conditionally applicable rules as criteria to evaluate the agent's reply for that situation. The judge is validated using human-verified synthetic golden dialogues. Benchmarking 8 LLMs on 1292 conversation turns reveals failure modes hidden by aggregate metrics: models with similar overall scores vary widely in their adherence to individual rules. All models struggle most with ambiguity clarification and Socratic questioning.

authors.name: Andrey Savchenko
authors.institution: National Research University Higher School of Economics

papers.title: Hybrid Cones: Set Representation with Sharp Unions of Minimal Overhead for Nonlinear and Switched Linear Systems
papers.abstract: Reachability analysis and set-based estimation for nonlinear systems require set representations capable of capturing nonconvex geometry. Hybrid Zonotopes (HZs) have recently gained attention because they can encode a union of up to $2^n$ polytopic components. Recent work has further shown that several HZ operations can be made \textit{sharp}, meaning that relaxing the binary variables yields exactly the convex hull of the represented set. However, no known HZ construction provides a sharp union of two convex sets that adds only one binary generator and no further continuous generators or equality constraints to those of the operands. This limitation affects scalability in repeated union operations, ReLU neural-network reachability, and nonlinear propagation methods that cover graph sets by unions of simpler sets. This paper identifies a connection between the exact closed-form convex-hull operation for Constrained Convex Generators (CCGs) and the binary-generator structure underlying HZs. We propose Hybrid Cones that can encode up to $2^n$ norm-cone components. Hybrid Cones inherit the logical structure of HZs while allowing richer convex components, including polytopic and norm-based sets. They support sharp unions requiring only one added binary variable and can represent unions and intersections of polytopes and ellipsoids. As a key application, we derive an exact representation of the ReLU graph using only two continuous and one binary generators. Numerical experiments for a localization problem with a nonlinear energy measurement function approximated by a neural network and the stability verification of the closed loop of a double integrator corrupted by a nonlinear disturbance with a saturated Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) controller show substantial reduction in representation size and reduced conservatism in comparison with HZs.

papers.title: On Mbekhta's conjecture and pseudo-Fredholm operators on Banach and Hilbert spaces
papers.abstract: We give negative answers to Mbekhta's conjecture \cite[p.~261]{Mbekhta} and to a related conjecture on pseudo-B-Fredholm operators \cite[p.~202]{AZO}. A sufficient condition for pseudo-Fredholmness on Banach spaces is established. It yields a characterization on Hilbert spaces in terms of the closedness of $\cc(T)$, $\cc(T)+\qn(T)$ and $\Ran(T)+\qn(T)$, as well as characterizations of pseudo-B-Fredholm and pseudo-B-Weyl operators on Banach spaces. A counterexample on a separable Banach space shows that the three closedness conditions do not characterize pseudo-Fredholmness in general. We also construct two operators having the same analytic core, quasinilpotent part, and kernels and ranges of all powers, although only one is pseudo-Fredholm. Moreover, a semi-B-Fredholm operator on a Banach space need not be a direct sum of a semi-Fredholm operator and a nilpotent operator, answering the question raised in \cite[p.~113]{AznayKato2023}. Finally, the three closedness conditions in the Hilbert-space characterization are shown to be independent.

papers.title: Integrated Sensing and Communication in 3GPP: Standardization, Performance Evaluation, and Experimental Validation Toward 6G
papers.abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is evolving from a primarily physical-layer research into a standardized cellular-network capability spanning channel modeling, radio procedures, network architecture, and the delivery of sensing services. We review this progression within the Third Generation Partnership Project (3GPP), from Release 19 service requirements and target-aware channel modeling to the Release 20 New Radio (NR) sensing evaluation framework, radio access network procedures, and system architecture, and discuss future directions toward 6G. We then present two 3GPP-aligned simulation case studies to demonstrate the corresponding evaluation approaches. The first case study compares hard-decision, soft-decision, and hybrid fusion for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) sensing using multiple transmission and reception points (TRPs). Detection, false alarms, and conditional position and velocity accuracy are evaluated using receiver-derived angle estimates and separately calibrated method-specific thresholds. The second case study compares ideal and practical sensing-assisted predictive handover with conventional handover, while accounting for sensing error and information age. We further present a testbed-based measurement study that characterizes monostatic and bistatic UAV radar cross sections across frequencies, platforms, and observation angles and provides empirical support for correlated target-response modeling. Finally, we discuss open challenges and future research directions in multi-node fusion, resource and interference management, network evolution, security, privacy, and reproducible evaluation. Together, these components connect calibrated channel models, link- and system-level simulation, real-time prototypes, controlled measurements, and field trials through a staged evaluation roadmap.

papers.title: Temporal vs Spectral Resolution in CSI Reporting for Wi-Fi ISAC
papers.abstract: CSI feedback is fundamental to proposed uses of Wi-Fi sensing such as human activity recognition (HAR); but it also constitutes significant overhead as resources must be allocated away from data communications. Wi-Fi CSI extraction can be explored along two dimensions in IEEE 802.11bf: reporting intensity, i.e., temporal resolution, and number of reported subcarriers, i.e., spectral resolution. We explore periodic and IEEE 802.11bf threshold-based reporting at matched rates, and uniform decimation and block-mean grouping at matched report sizes. We further propose reporting the mean CSI accumulated since the last report. Using the 802.11bf report size as the metric, we evaluate the accuracy-cost tradeoffs on three public datasets with our proposed model, a convolutional neural network combined with a gated recurrent unit and temporal pyramid pooling. The proposed periodic reporting with mean payload and block-mean grouping improves accuracy by up to 53 percentage points at equal CSI overhead cost. Temporal resolution is generally more cost-effective than spectral resolution. With only at most 7.7% of full-CSI feedback cost, the proposed scheme achieves 96-98% of full-CSI accuracy.

papers.title: Deep Learning for Deepfake Image Detection: Comparative Model Evaluation and Gradient-Based Visual Attribution
papers.abstract: Synthetic facial imagery has made the distinction between authentic and generated content increasingly important for digital forensics and online trust. This study examines an explainable deep-learning workflow for image-level deepfake detection using two contrasting classification strategies: a compact convolutional model trained from scratch and an ImageNet-pretrained MobileNetV2 model adapted through two-stage transfer learning. Experiments were conducted with the balanced 140k Real and Fake Faces dataset, comprising 140,000 facial images. Under the recorded validation protocol, the augmented from-scratch model reached 84.15% accuracy (loss 0.3625), compared with 95.90% accuracy (loss 0.1074) for the fine-tuned pretrained model. Gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) was used to visualize image regions associated with predictions, and a Flask-based prototype was developed for side-by-side inspection. These observations support the practical value of pretrained visual representations in the studied setting while underscoring the need to interpret validation performance alongside dataset provenance, explanation limitations, and evaluation scope. The reported results are validation results, not held-out test estimates.

papers.title: Nonrelativistic quantum theory of non-dipole effects in a multielectron atom: radiation transition operator
papers.abstract: In the work of Hopersky A.N. et al., arXiv: 2609.33494v1 [physics. atom-ph] in the Loudon integral representation, the general analytical structure of the complete operator of a multipole radiation transition taking into account non-dipole effects for a multielectron atom is established. In this Letter this structure is converted to the sum only for all multipoles.

papers.title: On the residual polynilpotence of tree products of groups with locally cyclic edge subgroups
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{N}$ be a non-empty class of nilpotent groups closed under taking subgroups, quotient groups, finite direct products, and unrestricted direct powers of the form $\prod_{x \in X}Y_{x}$, where $X \in \mathcal{N}$ and $Y_{x}$ ($x \in X$) are isomorphic copies of a group $Y \in \mathcal{N}$. Suppose also that $T$ is a tree product of $n$ groups ($2 \leqslant n < \infty$) with non-trivial torsion-free locally cyclic edge subgroups, $\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}}$ is the class of all torsion-free $\mathcal{N}$-groups, and the symbol $\mathit{Poly}_{k}\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}}$ ($k \geqslant 1$) denotes the class of polynilpotent groups such that $X \in \mathit{Poly}_{k}\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}}$ if and only if $X$ has a subnormal series of length at most $k$ whose factors belong to $\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}}$. We prove that if all free and all vertex groups are residually $\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}}$-groups, then $T$ is residually a $(\mathit{Poly}_{n+1}\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}})$-group. We prove also that if all vertex groups lie in $\mathcal{N}$, then $T$ has a homomorphism onto a $(\mathit{Poly}_{n-1}\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}})$-group acting injectively on all edge subgroups. By assuming that $\mathcal{N}$ is the class of all nilpotent groups, we get a stronger result: if all vertex groups are residually $\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}}$-groups, then $T$ is residually a $(\mathit{Poly}_{n}\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}})$-group. It follows that all cyclically-pinched one-relator groups are residually finitely generated $(\mathit{Poly}_{2}\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}})$-groups.

papers.title: ProtoGTX: Prototype-Aligned Graph Transformer for Explainable Whole-Slide Image Analysis
papers.abstract: Deep learning has achieved strong performance in computational pathology, but explaining whole-slide image (WSI) predictions remains challenging. Existing explanation methods often highlight important regions without identifying their morphological patterns, leaving a gap between patch-level computational evidence and slide-level pathological interpretation. We propose ProtoGTX, a graph-based framework that combines spatial contextualization with a flexible morphological prototype vocabulary. ProtoGTX separates the reference prototypes used to define morphological concepts from the predictive model: the reference vocabulary can be generated from training data by unsupervised clustering or supplied externally, and remains fixed during classifier training. Patch features are first contextualized over a spatial graph, after which learnable prototypes representing morphological concepts are optimized through cross-attention. Their slide-level activation profile is aligned with the morphological composition induced by the fixed reference prototype bank. On the CPTAC and BRACS datasets, ProtoGTX outperforms the evaluated MIL, prototype-based, and graph-based baselines, with particularly pronounced improvements on BRACS. Qualitative analyses further show that spatial contextualization transforms fragmented patch-level prototype assignments into more coherent tissue regions. In BRACS, prototype maps also co-localize with pathologist annotations and regions relevant to slide-level prediction. These results demonstrate that ProtoGTX provides complementary semantic and spatial explanations while retaining a prototype vocabulary that can be defined independently of the predictive model. Code is available at https://github.com/mizuno-group/ProtoGTX.

papers.title: ParetoChat: An LLM-Based Interface for Interactive Multi-Objective Optimization
papers.abstract: Multi-objective optimization models are often deployed in settings where decision makers (DMs) must balance some conflicting criteria. In practice, however, stakeholders must translate their qualitative preferences between different criteria into numerical weights, priorities, or reference points required by optimization methods, which can be difficult to specify and interpret. This paper proposes \emph{ParetoChat}, an LLM (large language model)-based expert-agent interface for interactive multi-objective optimization. The agent translates natural-language user input into structured scalarization parameters, invokes an optimization system, presents candidate solutions, and iteratively elicits feedback. We describe a multi-agent architecture that separates input processing, multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) expertise, solution presentation, and feedback processing. We then present a simulation study using an LLM-based DM agent and benchmark ParetoChat against interactive methods implemented in DESDEO, including reference-point and NIMBUS methods. The computational experiments on multi-objective binary knapsack and set-partitioning instances show that ParetoChat can guide the search efficiently toward solutions that match the DM's preferences. An application to historical courier-order assignment instances illustrates how users can explore objective extremes and intermediate trade-offs through natural-language requests. The results indicate that LLM agents may provide a practical interaction layer between business stakeholders and optimization tools.

papers.title: Acceleration Survives Heavy Tails and Generalized Smoothness
papers.abstract: We establish high-probability accelerated convergence guarantees for convex $(L_0,L_1)$-smooth optimization with unbiased stochastic gradients under heavy-tailed noise, assuming a central $α$-th noise moment bounded by $σ^α$, $α\in(1,2]$. Such guarantees are known under classical $L$-smoothness, but extending them through localization over an $O(R)$-radius ball may introduce an $e^{O(L_1R)}$ factor. We avoid this dependence in two ways. First, a two-phase scheme uses Clip-SGD to reach a low-curvature regime, after which clipped stochastic similar triangles (Clip-SSTM) attains, with probability at least $1-δ$, $f(y_K)-f^\star\le\widetilde{\mathcal O}\big(L_0R^2/K^2+σRK^{-(α-1)/α}\big),$ where $R$ bounds the distance from the Phase-II starting point to a minimizer. Second, a modified deterministic weight schedule allows Clip-SSTM to start directly from the initial point, controlling the high-curvature transient before recovering acceleration. With the prescribed initialization, both approaches recover the classical accelerated rate, with $L_1$ confined to an accuracy-independent transient, up to logarithmic factors.
