We further construct TrojanBench, a benchmark of 384 poisoned repositories spanning 6 domains and 9 programming languages. Extensive experiments show that TrojanForge achieves a stable poisoning success rate of over 60% with backdoor injection exceeding 90%. Comprehensive evaluation on TrojanBench across 4 harnesses and 12 models reveals that even commercial agents fail to defend against repository-level poisoning.

authors.name: Xiao Yang
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Jiawei Chen
authors.institution: Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Minimal asymptotic \(g\)-adic bases from arbitrary partitions
papers.abstract: Let $g>h\ge2$ be integers. For a nonempty set $W\subseteq\N$, let $\mathcal F^*(W)$ denote the set of its finite nonempty subsets. Let $$A_g(W)=\left\{\sum_{f\in F}a_fg^f: 1\leq a_f \leq g-1,F \in \mathcal F^*(W)\right\},$$ and let $\N=W_1\sqcup\cdots\sqcup W_h$ be a partition into infinite sets. We prove that $A=\bigcup_{i=1}^h A_g(W_i)$ is a minimal asymptotic basis of order $h$ for every such partition.

papers.title: Not All Test-Time Compute Is Evidence: Model-Specific Bias in LLM Reasoning
papers.abstract: Test-time scaling methods implicitly assume that additional computation from the same model provides independent evidence. We show that this assumption fails within a single reasoning model: errors are correlated across repeated samples, across reasoning depth, and in the model's own self-evaluation, so more compute from the same model is not more evidence. We introduce DIA (Disagreement-triggered Independent Arbitration), which treats disagreement between an intermediate-stage and the final-stage prediction as a per-question signal of reasoning instability and resolves it by asking a small panel of heterogeneous models to solve the question independently, without seeing either candidate, and aggregating their answers directly. Across seven benchmarks and two base models, DIA outperforms full chain-of-thought in 12 of 14 settings, including a 7.00% gain on MuSiQue, while activating on only $\sim 17\%$ of examples and using up to 47.2% fewer tokens than a multi-agent baseline. Ablations show that both independent solving and solver heterogeneity are necessary for these gains.

authors.name: Tianjun Yao
authors.institution: University of Shanghai for Science and Technology

papers.title: STC-MGNet: Spatial-Temporal-Channel Attention-Enhanced Multimodal Graph Network for Pedestrian Intention Prediction
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of pedestrian crossing intentions plays a critical role in enhancing the safety of pedestrian-vehicle interactions in autonomous driving. However, effectively capturing subtle spatiotemporal patterns in pedestrian pose sequences and integrating complementary visual and ego-vehicle motion information remain challenging. This paper proposes a spatial-temporal-channel attention-enhanced multimodal graph network (STC-MGNet) for pedestrian crossing intention prediction. STC-MGNet introduces a spatial-temporal-channel (STC) attention-enhanced pose graph encoder to learn discriminative representations from pedestrian pose sequences. Three parallel attention branches selectively emphasize informative skeletal joints, observation frames, and feature channels, with their outputs integrated through learnable fusion weights. To leverage complementary visual and ego-vehicle motion information, a multi-stage cross-modal channel modulation mechanism is introduced to adaptively refine pose representations through modality-specific channel gating at successive graph encoding stages. Experimental results demonstrate that STC-MGNet achieves accuracy rates of 70%, 87%, and 88% on the JAADbeh, JAADall, and PIE datasets, respectively, outperforming several representative baseline methods. Ablation experiments further highlight the complementary contributions of visual and ego-vehicle motion information to prediction performance.

papers.title: Monitor-Validity Failures: LLM Safety Evidence Paths at Evolving Framework Boundaries
papers.abstract: Modern LLM applications rely on runtime monitors that inspect tool calls, traces, streams, detector outputs, and verifier inputs. This creates an interface-reliability problem: a framework path may remain operational while policy-relevant evidence never reaches its decision point. In one representative case, a regex detector returned a positive match, but the framework stranded the result before the block decision. This differs from jailbreaks and detector errors because the evidence is already recognized yet disconnected from enforcement. We study this repair-boundary signature with canary contracts: parent/fixed confirmation units that place a known payload only on the changed evidence surface and record monitor visibility together with the downstream decision for action-boundary cases. Applying the protocol to public framework repairs, we confirm 18 evidence-path failures across 11 LLM or agent safety project groups and four implementation ecosystems. Nine are established-boundary repairs, eight are new-surface policy-coverage gaps, and one is a boundary-only evidence case. Fourteen reach E1 enforcement boundaries: seven native action outcomes, six configured enforcement boundaries, and one synthetic-consumer consequence. The remaining cases affect verifier, safety-prompt, or observability channels. The cases form carrier, adapter, authority, and surface families and show how ordinary application behavior can remain intact while a safety-specific evidence path misses its decision. Exact revisions, deterministic outcomes, negative controls, and a frozen prospective audit document the confirmation rule. Monitor assumptions therefore need regression tests at the schemas, streams, tools, and adapters that frameworks evolve.

authors.name: Junchi Liao
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Three-circle inequalities for almost harmonic functions on cylinders
papers.abstract: The three-circle method was introduced into the blow-up analysis of harmonic maps by Qing and Tian [Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 1997]. We extend this method to a class of $(τ,ε)$-almost harmonic functions on long cylinders and establish three-circle inequalities for their weighted energies. These inequalities yield a dichotomy between exponential energy decay and asymptotic dominance of a critical Fourier mode, together with a characterization of the corresponding normalized limiting profiles. In the unweighted case, we prove convergence of the averaged neck curves and identify their limiting equations under additional structural assumptions. Applications include neck analysis and energy identities for harmonic maps, solutions of Rivière's equation, $α$-harmonic maps, biharmonic approximations of harmonic maps, and Willmore surfaces.

papers.title: Agentic Physics-Grounded Video Generation via Memory-Augmented In-Context Reasoning
papers.abstract: Physical plausibility is essential for realistic video generation. Existing methods impose physical guidance before synthesis via simulations or refined prompts, but this can limit dynamic diversity, miss errors that emerge only after generation, and require repeated regeneration when inconsistencies remain. We therefore study a generate-diagnose-repair paradigm that preserves the original generation capability and selectively repairs physical inconsistencies afterward, raising two key questions: what to repair and how to repair? To address them, we introduce PhysRepair, an agentic video generation framework that combines causal reasoning over the observed physical failure with prior repair experience to enable localized and adaptive correction. Specifically, Spatiotemporal Causal Constraints identify the first invalid physical state and its causally affected states, producing a repair specification that guides physically plausible local regeneration while preserving unaffected content. Experience-augmented In-context Learning combines the ongoing repair context with relevant experience from previous repairs, allowing the agent to adapt its repair decisions across diverse physical failures and accumulate completed trajectories for future cases. Experiments on Physics-IQ Verified across solid mechanics, fluid dynamics, optics, thermodynamics, and magnetism demonstrate that PhysRepair consistently improves the physical plausibility of generated videos over existing methods. Our project page is available at https://xxkkxxx.github.io/PhysRepair-Website/.

authors.name: Can Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Kai Chen
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Beyond Explicit Intent: Discovering and Shaping Artistic Intent through Human-AI Co-Creation
papers.abstract: Generative AI is becoming an important medium for artistic creation, yet existing interactions often assume that creators can specify intentions in advance and accurately communicate them through text prompts. Artistic intentions, however, may be vague, latent, or recognizable only after seeing concrete visual possibilities. We propose a human-AI co-creation paradigm beyond explicit intent expression. By expanding model exploration, we expose artists to diverse visual possibilities, allowing them to identify previously unarticulated preferences through observation, comparison, and selection. We then integrate artists' curatorial judgments into reinforcement learning, assigning different learning strengths based on preferences over generation trajectories, so recognized directions are more strongly reinforced and the model gradually adapts to individual aesthetics. This creates a continuous "explore-identify-shape-re-explore" loop in which artistic intent is progressively discovered, externalized, and shaped. Through three user studies, we examine latent-preference discovery, personalized preference alignment, and the externalization of vague, difficult-to-express creative intentions.

authors.name: Yi Gao
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Explicit construction of optimal binary linear complementary pairs via Belov codes
papers.abstract: The study of linear complementary pairs (LCPs) has been a hot topic in coding theory. Recently, Güneri constructed an infinite family of optimal binary LCPs from Solomon-Stiffler codes. Specifically, he proved that for every $k \geq 5$ and $d \geq \lceil (k - 1)/2 \rceil 2^{k - 1}$, there exist optimal binary linear complementary pairs of codes of length $g_2(k,d)$, where $g_2(k,d)$ denotes the Griesmer bound. In this paper, we construct additional optimal binary LCPs from Belov codes, which form a generalized class of Solomon-Stiffler codes. Our results not only generalize Güneri's construction, but also enable more flexible construction of optimal binary LCPs with a wide range of minimum distances.

authors.name: Yansheng Wu
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Sparsity-Corrected Tensor Clustering for Multi-Layer Networks
papers.abstract: Multi-layer networks provide complementary views of interactions among the same set of nodes. In practice, layers with similar community structures may have substantially different network sparsity, causing sparsity variation to obscure the structural patterns of interest. To address this problem, a sparsity heterogeneous mixture multi-layer stochastic block model is proposed, which separates layer-specific sparsity from group-specific community structure. Based on the induced low-rank tensor representation, a sparsity-corrected tensor clustering method is proposed to remove the layer-specific scale effect before clustering, without explicitly estimating the sparsity parameters. Theoretical guarantees for tensor decomposition, layer clustering, and community detection are established. The results further characterize the range of sparsity heterogeneity allowed for consistent recovery, including regimes where the sparsity ratio diverges with the network dimensions. Numerical studies and an application to international trade networks from BACI demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method under heterogeneous layer sparsity.

papers.title: Process Reward Modeling with Reliability- and Conservatism-Aware Bayesian Belief
papers.abstract: Process Reward Models (PRMs) play a central role in test-time scaling for large language model (LLM) reasoning. However, PRMs may provide inaccurate process rewards for test-time scaling, which we identify as arising from two sources of uncertainty: (1) \textit{PRM uncertainty} that arises from insufficient supervision data and imperfect PRM training; and (2) \textit{policy uncertainty} that results from the mismatch between the policy to collect supervision data and the policy for test-time scaling, leading to systematic reward overestimation. Previous studies fail to jointly consider both uncertainties. To bridge this gap, we propose BayesianPRM, which treats the process reward as a random variable within a reward hypothesis space and maintains a Bayesian belief over it. Since exact Bayesian inference over the continuous hypothesis space is generally intractable, we discretize the reward hypothesis space with a reward ensemble and introduce two complementary belief updates, each targeting one source of uncertainty: (1) to address PRM uncertainty, we introduce \textit{reliability-aware belief updating} that measures how well each ensemble member explains the supervision data and updates the belief with an amortized belief network optimized by the evidence lower bound (ELBO); and (2) to tackle policy uncertainty, we propose \textit{conservatism-aware belief calibration} which further reweights the belief toward lower rewards to suppress overestimation. These two updates yield a reliability- and conservatism-aware Bayesian belief, whose expectation determines the process reward. Experiments on multimodal reasoning benchmarks indicate that BayesianPRM consistently yields more accurate process reward estimates while enhancing test-time scaling performance.

papers.title: Interfacial Faraday instability driven by interspecies-interaction modulation in a phase-separated binary Bose-Einstein condensate
papers.abstract: We investigate interfacial Faraday instabilities in a quasi-two-dimensional, phase-separated binary Bose-Einstein condensate driven by periodic modulation of the interspecies scattering length. In the strongly immiscible regime, the interspecies interaction energy is concentrated near the internal interface, linking the modulation to interfacial tension and the capillary restoring force. We quantify the first-order tension response through its logarithmic sensitivity and account for nonlinear tension variations at finite modulation amplitudes. A sharp-interface capillary model and Floquet analysis yield discrete azimuthal-mode frequencies and primary instability tongues that shift toward higher driving frequencies with increasing mode order. Gross-Pitaevskii simulations reveal star-shaped interface patterns with threefold to eightfold rotational symmetry. The eightfold mode exhibits subharmonic oscillations and approximately exponential growth of its period-averaged amplitude over a small-deformation interval. These results provide a route to frequency-selective excitation of interfacial capillary modes through interspecies-interaction control.

authors.name: Yan Li

papers.title: Brauer-Manin obstruction for symmetric powers
papers.abstract: For a quasi-projective smooth geometrically integral variety $X$ over a number field, we prove that the Brauer-Manin obstruction for its symmetric powers coincides with the obstruction coming from $X$. As a consequence, Brauer-Manin obstruction for the symmetric powers cannot provide new cohomological obstruction to weak approximation of zero-cycles for $X$. The key intermediate ingredients are a Dold-Thom type result for Brauer groups and a precise descent formula for adelic points.

authors.name: Yang Cao
authors.institution: Hunan University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

papers.title: "You" Is Not Toxic: How LLM Labelers Rewrite the Web's Conversation Laws
papers.abstract: What the Web community believes about toxic conversations, such as that toxicity rises in longer and deeper threads, was measured mostly with Google's Perspective API, which is shutting down; large language models (LLMs) will make the next measurements. We find that LLM labelers mistake second-person address for toxicity, and that this one bias manufactures laws that human labels do not show. On 1.25 million news comments with crowd labels, Claude Haiku flags 12% of the non-toxic comments that contain no "you" and 51% of those with four or more; a single crowd rater flags 6% and 10%. Deeper replies address someone more often, so under Haiku toxicity rises with reply depth (+0.93 percentage points per level), while under the crowd's labels it slightly declines (-0.12). Rewriting "you" in the third person removes two thirds of the false rise; flagging only as many comments as the crowd does not remove it, and showing Haiku the parent comment enlarges it. All seven LLMs we test over-flag "you", and at the crowd's flag rate, without the parent, any false rise of the open ones vanishes at a fixed number of second-person words; Haiku also over-flags "you" on Reddit, Gab and Wikipedia talk pages. Agreement with human labels does not reveal the bias: we prove that a fixed Cohen's kappa leaves a law nearly unconstrained. We therefore certify the law instead of the labeler. Threadsafe uses the labeler's scores to choose which comments human raters label and to predict the others, and corrects the predictions with the human labels; linear laws are estimated without bias whatever the labeler does. In simulated audits its intervals for the laws keep nominal coverage from 250 labels on, where uniform-sample methods such as PPI++ fall short, and at 1,000 to 8,000 labels are 0.75 times as wide as those of design-based supervised learning (DSL); a thousand human labels rule out Haiku's rising law.

papers.title: Perceive, Solve, Reason: Progressive Capability Formation in Time Series-LLMs
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can now perceive, describe, and reason about images and audio, yet time series understanding remains underestimated: most work uses LLMs as forecasters and classifiers, reasoning studies are few and narrow, and no suite trains and evaluates the full range of capabilities. In this paper, we build the first such suite, with 337K training and 44K evaluation samples across three progressive capabilities, Perceive, Solve, and Reason, and use it to ask how time series should enter an LLM that must master all three, and in what order. We find that a dedicated encoder is essential: with one, a 4B model surpasses GPT-4o on every perception attribute we test, whereas textualizing the series costs 8--10 points in reasoning accuracy. The capabilities then build on one another: learning them in order beats mixing the same data and rivals reasoning-only training with over three times the reasoning data, but only when an encoder is used. Analyses further reveal that capabilities are transferred through distinct network depths rather than simply stacked, and that a stage converged on its own benchmark is not necessarily ready for the next. Distilled into a simple recipe, these findings yield 4B TS-LLMs that, without any target-domain data, outperform four recent 7B TS-LLMs on seven of eight out-of-domain metrics, by up to 11 points. We therefore advocate treating time series as a first-class modality for LLMs, read through dedicated encoders and taught to perceive before they reason.

papers.title: Deligne--Faltings Logarithmic Derived Geometry with a View towards Logarithmic GLSM
papers.abstract: Many perfect obstruction theories and virtual cycles in enumerative geometry are shadows from derived geometry. In this paper, we give a general construction of reduced perfect obstruction theories arising from a geometric reduction of the derived stack $X$ with respect to a $(-1)$-shifted log function $w_α$. Notably, this construction leads to a decomposition of the virtual cycle $[X]^{\mathrm{vir}}$ into the reduced virtual cycle $[X]^{\mathrm{red}}$ and a reduced boundary cycle $[Δ_X]^\red$. Our construction is motivated by future applications to the moduli stack of UMD logarithmic R-maps in log GLSM \cite{CJR21}. Along the way, we develop logarithmic analogs of several constructions in derived geometry, in particular proving a logarithmic Lagrangian intersection theorem.

papers.title: Under the Skin: Backdoor Infection in Multimodal Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have achieved impressive performance in generating text conditioned on inputs from different modalities. In this work, we introduce backdoor infection, a cross-modal attack framework targeting MLLMs. Starting from a model already injected with a backdoor in one modality, our attack constructs a corresponding trigger in another modality, called the infected modality. Exploiting the model's shared latent space, the trigger in the infected modality reliably activates the malicious behavior, without modifying or poisoning the infected modality during training. We further develop a lightweight, constraint-aware optimization method for efficient and practical trigger generation. Extensive experiments across several state-of-the-art MLLMs, including LLaVA, InternVL, Qwen-VL, and Gemma, demonstrate that our approach identifies cross-modal triggers that are more efficient, effective, and less detectable than direct optimization baselines, highlighting a critical new threat vector in multimodal systems.

papers.title: From Sliding Windows to Self-evolving Lifelong Memory: A Dual-perspective Survey of Memory Paradigms for Long-Horizon Robotics VLA Models
papers.abstract: Long-horizon robotic tasks expose a fundamental limitation of current Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models because their restricted temporal context pre-vents effective accumulation and reuse of past experiences. As a result, memory has become a fundamental component for enabling embodied agents to perform long-horizon reasoning and adaptive decision-making. This survey presents a systematic taxonomy of VLA memory mechanisms based on memory scope and persistence, categorizing existing approaches into five representative paradigms and one emerging frontier. Based on this taxonomy, we compare representative VLA memory systems in terms of memory characteristics, architectural com-plexity, and open-source maturity, revealing a clear trade-off in which increasing architectural complexity is generally accompanied by decreasing open-source ma-turity. Finally, we discuss the key challenges in building full-lifecycle memory systems, including efficient memory management and lifelong knowledge evolu-tion. Overall, this survey provides a unified perspective on memory architectures for VLA agents and offers insights into the development of lifelong embodied in-telligence.

authors.name: Keyuan Luo
authors.institution: Hainan Bielefeld University of Applied Sciences

papers.title: Beyond Large Language Models: A Mental World Model Framework for Mental Modeling, Simulation, Evolution, and Interpretability
papers.abstract: Understanding and simulating how subjective cognition and mental states emerge, evolve, and shape behavior is essential for advancing artificial intelligence toward deeper social cognition and general intelligence. Existing large language models (LLMs) and Theory of Mind (ToM) methods primarily infer mental states from linguistic information, lacking unified mechanisms for subjective world construction, cognitive-psychological interactions, dynamic evolution, and historical dependencies. This paper introduces the Mental World Model (MWM) and its implementation, the Multi-Branch Mental Evolution Architecture (MMEA), which explicitly constructs subjective worlds, models interactions between cognition and mental states, and simulates continuous mental evolution shaped by historical experiences. On DynToM and RecToM, MMEA achieves 96.48% and 94.00% accuracy, respectively, outperforming leading LLMs and specialized ToM methods. Additional experiments demonstrate improvements of 28.7, 39.3, and 16.6 percentage points in mental state and behavior prediction, long-sequence prediction, and implicit mental state inference, respectively. The results demonstrate that MMEA provides an interpretable framework for continuous mental modeling, enabling AI to move beyond surface-level semantic representations to infer individuals' underlying mental states from linguistic information and dynamically simulate their internal cognitive processes and evolution over time. MWM also provides a promising foundation for causal reasoning, personalized AI, sustained human-AI interaction, and future advances toward artificial general intelligence (AGI).

papers.title: Optimal subsampling approach for Cox models under large-scale length-biased right-censored data
papers.abstract: With the rapid advancement of data acquisition technologies, massive survival data have become increasingly prevalent, posing substantial computational challenges for the standard Cox proportional hazards model under complex censoring and truncation mechanisms. This paper addresses the analysis of large-scale length-biased right-censored data within the Cox model framework. We propose a novel subsampling approach to enhance computational efficiency for large samples and establish theoretically that the resulting subsample estimator provides an efficient approximation to the full-data estimator, while preserving consistency and asymptotic normality. Explicit optimal subsampling probabilities are derived under A- and L-optimality criteria. To facilitate practical implementation, we develop an efficient two-step estimation algorithm. Extensive numerical simulations and an empirical analysis of U.S. airline flight operation data evaluate the estimation performance and computational gains under various censoring rates and sample sizes. The results demonstrate that the proposed method substantially reduces computational cost while preserving statistical accuracy, offering a practical and scalable solution for analyzing large-scale length-biased right-censored survival data.

authors.name: Jianhua Shi
authors.institution: First Affiliated Hospital of Xi'an Jiaotong University

papers.title: Interplay between high-entropy effects and the superionic transition in fluorite oxides: A liquid-like perspective
papers.abstract: Minor actinide (MA)-bearing mixed oxide (MOX), a prominent high-entropy ceramic (HEC), is a promising candidate for advanced fast reactor fuels. Using a hybrid Monte Carlo/Molecular Dynamics (MC/MD) approach, we reveal that Np and Am segregation establishes a distinct short-range order (SRO) that induces severe lattice distortion. We uncover a competitive mechanism between localized high-entropy blocking effects and collective superionic dynamics, where the anionic kinetic and structural evolution within the 2000-2800 K range is partitioned and governed by the Tammann crossover temperature and superionic transition temperature. In the low-temperature regime, severe lattice distortions induced by the SRO structures create localized electrostatic and strain-coupled potential wells, which spatially confine the O-ions and lead to their sluggish diffusion. The system exhibits increased dynamical heterogeneity as thermal activation alleviates these structural constraints. Crucially, these localized traps spontaneously transform into a highly interconnected, string-like polyhedral topological network. Driven by the maximization of configurational entropy, this structural change creates low-viscosity transport pathways that trigger confinement-enhanced diffusion. Consequently, a dramatic kinetic inversion occurs, where the O-ion mobility of SRO model surpasses that of random solid solution (RSS) model via an entropy-driven compensation mechanism. Finally, through Gibbs free energy minimization and defect analysis, structural and thermodynamic origins of the superionic transition in HEC are elucidated. This study unveils how local chemical ordering regulates ion transport under extreme conditions, providing theoretical support for the design of high-performance nuclear fuels with both superior radiation tolerance and optimized mass transfer capabilities.

papers.title: AcousticAgent: A Floorplan-Centric Simulation Platform for Distributed Multi-Room Speech Processing
papers.abstract: Existing acoustic simulation tools either generate room impulse responses (RIRs) efficiently in parameterized rooms or rely on preconstructed three-dimensional scenes, making it difficult to build large numbers of editable residential multi-room environments. We present AcousticAgent, a floorplan-centric acoustic simulation platform that converts structured floorplans into editable, acoustically connected multi-room scenes. AcousticAgent jointly models room geometry and connectivity, furniture, materials, sound sources, and microphone configurations. A scene-oriented Acoustic Materials Database maps semantic elements to acoustic parameters, while a floorplan-aware hybrid geometrical-acoustics solver generates multichannel RIRs and reverberant audio. The platform also supports directional and moving sources, distributed microphones, and VLM-assisted scene construction from floorplan images and text. Using AcousticAgent, we construct FP-RIR, a dataset covering 15,376 residential floorplans with diverse room topologies, propagation conditions, and source--receiver configurations. We validate its acoustic fidelity against real-world measurements and evaluate whole-home source localization, speech enhancement, and far-field speech processing under single-device and distributed microphone settings. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of floorplan-aware modeling for large-scale residential acoustic simulation and the benefits of distributed spatial processing in multi-room environments. AcousticAgent and FP-RIR provide scalable and configurable resources for developing and evaluating residential speech systems.

papers.title: Unified Geometric--Kinematic Laws of Mobility in 3D Cellular Networks
papers.abstract: Mobility in three-dimensional (3D) cellular networks induces frequent handovers and random sojourn times for aerial users. Analyzing these events is challenging because they jointly depend on user trajectories and random service-boundary geometry. This paper develops a unified geometric--kinematic framework in which service regions form a stationary random tessellation, their boundaries constitute a random closed set, and user motion follows a cruise--turn mobility model. Under the stated stationarity, isotropy, and independence conditions, the handover rate satisfies the exact law \(H=(S_V/2)\bar v\), where \(S_V\) is the specific surface area and \(\bar v\) is the long-run mean speed. The forward boundary-distance distribution provides the local geometric input to an effective-traversal approximation for the mean remaining sojourn time. These results link global and local geometric descriptors to complementary mobility metrics. Combining the handover law with link coverage yields a handover-aware effective spectral efficiency for base station (BS) density selection and service-architecture comparison. We then specialize the framework to Poisson--Voronoi single-BS service and Poisson--Delaunay four-BS coordinated multi-point service; under both models, the handover rate scales as \(λ^{1/3}\bar v\). Numerical results corroborate the exact handover expressions, assess the sojourn-time approximations, and show how user speed and interruption duration affect the preferred density and architecture.

papers.title: LY-GWM-RoboCasa-Human300: Prediction-Guided Action Selection with a Graph Dynamics Model
papers.abstract: We present LY-GWM-RoboCasa-Human300, a policy that combines a Human300-fine-tuned GR00T-N1.5 action generator, an action-conditioned graph dynamics model, and a learned binary state-reward scorer. At inference, the policy samples four action chunks, predicts the future latent features and robot state for each, and executes the candidate with the highest predicted-state reward logit. Predictions therefore influence the actions sent to the environment. The evaluated system uses a 16-step prediction horizon and keeps all three components frozen during evaluation. In the local evaluation on 50 RoboCasa 1.0.1 tasks in the pretrain kitchen split, with 50 episodes per task, the system records 207/2,500 successes (8.28%), compared with 181/2,500 (7.24%) in the historical self-trained GR00T-N1.5 baseline. The observed difference is 26 successes, or 1.04 percentage points. The atomic group improves from 141/900 to 150/900. Separately, the RoboCasa maintainers re-evaluated the submission and reported 354/1,500 successes (23.6%) across 50 tasks, with leaderboard rates of 48.3%, 16.3%, and 3.1% for Atomic-Seen, Composite-Seen, and Composite-Unseen. The local and official results are reported separately; their difference is not attributed to a model improvement. Recorded local audits identify 212,700 changed environment-input chunks, including 28,223 in atomic tasks. We describe the actual training stages, implemented inference mechanism, evaluation provenance, and public reproduction entrypoints. These results document an active prediction-and-selection system and a positive historical difference.

papers.title: Subvariety intervals and limit varieties of zero extensions of mirror-word semirings
papers.abstract: For the mirror word $\mathbf{m}_n=a_1\cdots a_na_n\cdots a_1$, let $\mathcal{V}_n=\mathrm{V}(S(\mathbf{m}_n))$ and $\mathcal{W}_n=\mathrm{V}(S(\mathbf{m}_n)^0)$. We show that $[\mathcal{W}_n,\mathcal{W}_{n+1}]$ ($n\geq 1$) and $[\mathcal{V}_n,\mathcal{W}_n]$ ($n\geq 2$) have cardinality $2^{\aleph_0}$. Every variety in $[\mathcal{W}_2,\mathcal{W}_\infty]$ has infinite axiomatic rank. The unique limit subvariety of $\mathcal{W}_1$ is $\mathrm{V}(SR_6)$. For $n\geq 2$, we construct a distinct directed-path limit variety contained in $\mathcal{W}_n$ but not in $\mathcal{V}_n$.

papers.title: CoLU: Confidence-Weighted Layerwise Unlearning for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) unlearning aims to forget certain information while preserving others, without retraining from scratch. SoTA methods such as NPO, SimNPO, and SatImp balance forgetting and retain through whole model fine-tuning, while FOM-UL explores selective layer updates. Prior works show that suppressing target information can damage retained knowledge. This trade-off can vary across layers even under the same unlearning loss. In this work, we propose Confidence-Weighted Layerwise Unlearning (CoLU), which combines a novel confidence-weighted forgetting and retain regularization while updating a single selected transformer layer, rather than the whole model for unlearning. To reduce CoLU compute cost, we further propose Brief Layer Screening (BLS), which uses a newly defined normalized forgetting-retention (NFR) score to first rank layers through a brief unlearning trials using a subset of forgetting dataset and fewer epochs. BLS pre-selects top-k ranked layer candidates, which will then be fully profiled using full data analysis. BLS is proven to reduce the runtime of CoLU by 60.2-79.7% with almost the same performance. On TOFU dataset, CoLU improves both forgetting and retention over NPO, SatImp, and GA-based FOM-UL in all six TOFU settings, and over SimNPO in five of the six settings. On MUSE Books and News datasets, CoLU achieves the highest retained KnowMem and the PrivLeak closest to zero among the compared SOTA unlearning methods. CoLU presents a new record performance in both unlearning and retain in most settings up to date. Moreover, across the measured settings, average CoLU GPU memory usage is 77.4% to 79.5% lower than full-model unlearning.

papers.title: Variational and Decomposed method for Mitigating Bimodal Bias in Robust Visual Question Answering
papers.abstract: Visual question answering (VQA) models are known to suffer from the bias issue, which refers to overfitting the regularities of frequent patterns. Previously, researchers only consider the language bias. Recently, the multimodal bias is noticed. However, what multimodal bias is remains unclear. In this paper, we investigate the multimodal bias in counting and non-counting questions. We find that they have distinct underlying mechanism, so their biases come from distinct reasons. We provide valuable interpretations of VQA counting mechanism: \textbf{quantity information stems from the magnitude of the multimodal features in specific dimensions.} Thus, counting bias stems from the vision side and propagates to multimodal features through modality fusion, while the non-counting bias stems from primarily language bias and slightly vision bias. Thus, we propose a method to deal with them differently: Variational and Decomposed method for mitigating Bimodal Bias (VDB). It extracts bimodal bias affected by different proportion of vision and language sides. We introduce variational bias models utilizing the principle of Variational Auto-Encoder to learn mainly language bias with slight vision effect, and a bimodal bias model for bimodal bias combining language and vision sides. Extensive experiments on VQACPv2, VQACPv1, and GQAOOD datasets demonstrate the rationality of our claim and the effectiveness of our method. We also provide explanation for the compromised performance on VQAv2.

authors.name: Yihan Zhao
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: ToPA: Block-wise Toeplitz Adaptation for Expressive and Efficient Fine-Tuning
papers.abstract: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) has emerged as a prevalent strategy for adapting large pre-trained models. Among PEFT techniques, reparameterization-based methods, particularly those that employ low-rank or sparsity structures, have attracted significant attention. However, these approaches often underperform full fine-tuning. Specifically, low-rank methods constrain the update rank, which is misaligned with the inherently high-rank nature of full fine-tuning. In contrast, sparsity-based techniques limit the flexibility of the parameter space and compromise connectivity across weights. To overcome these limitations, we explore the use of Toeplitz matrices, whose entries are constant along each diagonal, therefore providing a compact parameterization without imposing explicit rank or sparsity constraints. A straightforward approach is to update weights via a product of Toeplitz matrices. However, similar to RNNs, long multiplicative chains often lead to gradient instability. To address this issue, we propose \textbf{ToPA}, a more refined version of this idea that replaces standard Toeplitz matrices with block-wise Toeplitz, greatly increasing each factor's capacity and shortening the chain, thereby stabilizing training and improving expressiveness. We theoretically show that products of block-wise Toeplitz matrices can approximate arbitrary matrices under shorter chain length, justifying the structural design of ToPA. Furthermore, we demonstrate that ToPA offers greater expressivity than existing low-rank and sparse parameterizations. Empirical evaluations across 21 NLP and CV datasets, spanning 5 model architectures, consistently validate the effectiveness of ToPA.

papers.title: Scalable Levenberg-Marquardt Training Framework for Deep Learning
papers.abstract: The Levenberg-Marquardt (LMA) algorithm is a widely used nonlinear least-squares solver known for its rapid convergence. For small-scale neural networks, LMA provides better convergence and architectural robustness than first-order optimizers like Adam. However, LMA imposes prohibitive memory and computational costs. These costs are primarily from the Jacobian matrix, whose dimensions scale with both the number of samples and parameters. This bottleneck prevents its use in large-scale neural networks. Recent efforts scale LMA using preconditioned conjugate gradient (PCG) solvers to avoid materializing the Jacobian. However, PCG only approximates the solution, requiring many network propagations and a task-specific preconditioner. Other studies optimize LMA to reduce costs, but they restrict their methods to specific tasks or network architectures. As a result, LMA remains impractical for training general large-scale neural networks. In this paper, we propose LeMA, a distributed LMA algorithm for large-scale neural network training on multi-GPU platforms. Our contributions are twofold: First, an exact dual formulation of LMA removes the memory dependence on the parameter dimension. Second, a Jacobian sharding strategy computes Jacobian shards on the fly and in parallel to avoid materializing the full Jacobian. For large-scale neural networks, LeMA reduces the memory footprint of LMA from quadratic in the number of parameters to quadratic in the batch size. This makes exact LMA steps feasible for billion-parameter models without approximate PCG solves. Furthermore, for a convolutional neural network with 1,000,022,632 parameters on an 8-GPU node, LeMA achieves a 7.97x speedup over a single GPU, corresponding to a 99.7% strong scaling efficiency.

papers.title: Perron--Wright asymptotics and critical component processes for inhomogeneous random graphs
papers.abstract: We extend Wright's enumeration of connected labelled graphs with fixed surplus to irreducible critical finite type kernels and continuous compact type kernels satisfying a positivity condition. Let $\mathsf{C}_t(k,r)$ denote the total weight of connected labelled graphs with $k$ vertices and surplus $r$. Let $u>0$ satisfy $Ku=u$ and $\int u dμ=1$, and put $α=\int u^2 dμ$ and $β=\int u^3 dμ$. We prove that the rooted-tree radius $ρ$ is positive and real analytic near $1$, with $ρ(1)=1$ and $\logρ(t)=\frac{α^2}{2β}(t-1)^2+O(|t-1|^3)$, and that, for fixed $r\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$ and $0\le L<\infty$, $\mathsf{C}_t(k,r)=w_rβ^{(r-1)/2}e^{-k}ρ(t)^{-k}k^{k+3r/2-2}\{1+O_{r,L}(k^{-1/2})\}$, uniformly for $|t-1|\le Lk^{-1/2}$, where $w_r$ is the classical Wright constant. At criticality, the leading constant depends on the kernel only through $β$, under the stated normalization of $u$. At $t_n=1+λn^{-1/3}$, exact component identities combine with these asymptotics to give fixed size factorial densities and local size and surplus point-process limits for deterministic finite type models and annealed compact type Bollobás-Janson-Riordan models. With sizes rescaled by $β^{1/3}n^{-2/3}$, the limit is the Aldous process at parameter $αβ^{-2/3}λ$, and the corresponding type profiles concentrate at the Perron law $p(dx)=u(x)μ(dx)$. For every bounded uniformly positive countable critical kernel, we construct graph sequences with growing finite supports and the same local limits, and identify the additive shift of the critical window caused by spectral perturbations of order $n^{-1/3}$.

papers.title: VLA-Fabric: Learning Interaction for Composable Multi-Arm VLA Agents
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models are rapidly expanding what individual robots can accomplish, yet many real-world manipulation settings require multiple arms to operate as a coordinated system. Existing approaches organize multi-arm coordination in different ways, including centralized joint policies, high-level task or role assignment, and locally executed policies that react to teammates. However, how complete action-producing VLAs should explicitly interact with one another during action generation remains largely unexplored. We introduce VLA-Fabric, which organizes one complete VLA per arm while preserving local perception and action ownership, and enables coordination through learned interaction across policy boundaries. We first systematically study where such interaction should occur, how peer information should be aggregated, and how the interaction should be learned, revealing complementary coordination functions spanning shared context, peer-specific latent information, and action-stage interaction. We then re-instantiate these functions in a structurally different VLA architecture, showing that the coordination principle is not tied to a particular tensor layout or backbone implementation. Finally, we compose teams of three and four arms and evaluate them in simulation and physical experiments. On all four physical tasks, Full interaction improves success over independently trained local policies by 16--40 percentage points. Together, these results suggest that explicit interaction among complete VLA policies offers a scalable path toward networked embodied intelligence.

papers.title: Nonconvex Carnot Limit Shapes for Branching Random Walks on the Heisenberg Group
papers.abstract: We study a supercritical branching random walk on the discrete Heisenberg group driven by the four standard horizontal generators. Horizontal position has scale $n$, whereas the central coordinate records discrete area and has scale $n^2$. On the Galton-Watson survival event, we prove almost sure Hausdorff convergence, under Carnot scaling, of both the rescaled particle positions and the collections of enhanced ancestral paths. The path limit consists of area lifts of horizontal paths $ω$ satisfying $J_t(ω)\le t\logρ$ for every $t\in[0,1]$, where $ρ$ is the offspring mean. In contrast to the classical Euclidean case, the deterministic limit shape is nonconvex for every $ρ>1$. We identify its horizontal projection and interval vertical fibers, determine the saturated shape for $ρ\ge4$, and characterize the origin fiber below saturation by Wulff duality. A hyperbolic representation gives an elliptic integral formula for the Wulff area. The maximal central coordinate $Γ_ρ$ is nondecreasing and concave in $ρ$, equals $1/4$ for $ρ\ge4$, and satisfies $Γ_ρ=(\logρ)/π-(\logρ)^2/(4π) +O((\logρ)^3)$ as $ρ\downarrow1$. For fixed $1<ρ<4$, we obtain $M_n^Z=Γ_ρn^2+O(n^{3/2}\sqrt{\log n})$ almost surely. Above saturation the first correction is a random linear term; at $ρ=4$, under a finite second moment assumption, the deficit $Γ_4n^2-M_n^Z$ has order $n\log\log n$ in probability.

authors.name: Bohan Hu
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Enhancing Visual Task-Redirection Attacks on Vision-Language-Action Models via Closed-Loop Optimization
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable language-guided robot manipulation, but remain vulnerable to visual attacks that undermine user control over robot behavior. Prior studies optimize visual perturbations using fixed target supervision. However, the perturbation can change earlier actions and, in turn, the physical states reached later. As the attacked trajectory evolves, this supervision may no longer match the behavior needed at the states actually reached. Accurately matching these targets can therefore fail to advance the attacker-specified task. Even with suitable supervision, reducing average matching error does not ensure sustained task progress. The robot may still fail at a critical stage, and further updates can disrupt previously successful behavior. To address these limitations, we propose TRACO, a framework that enhances existing targeted visual attacks through closed-loop optimization. Its Execution-Driven Supervision rebuilds supervision for the states reached under attack to guide subsequent updates. Within this framework, Progress-Guided Selection focuses updates where progress stalls while maintaining supervision on the earlier behavior needed to reach that point. Experiments across VLA models and simulation environments show improved task-redirection success with TRACO, highlighting the security implications of closed-loop attack optimization.

authors.name: Guanying Chen
authors.institution: Ministry of Industry and Information Technology

authors.name: Jianhao Chen
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: MARS: Memory-Aware Routing for Session-Level LLM Assistants
papers.abstract: Long-term LLM assistants must repeatedly decide what prior context to expose and which model should answer as an interaction evolves. Existing memory systems and model routers usually make these decisions separately, although memory construction changes the evidence, distractors, and difficulty of the resulting input. We introduce MARS, a memory-aware routing framework that uses session state as a shared control interface between memory construction and model selection. A Query and Topic Manager (QTM) estimates compact decision-relevant state that guides a fixed state-conditioned memory policy and an online router, enabling each turn to receive an appropriate memory view and a suitable model under a quality-memory-cost trade-off. We evaluate MARS on RealMem and MultiChallenge with 16 system configurations each, covering long-history memory-driven interaction and bounded sessions with structured context interference. On RealMem, MARS preserves 98.2% of full-context GPT-4o's QA while using only 14.5% of its generation API cost, including both generation and controller calls for MARS, and achieves the strongest measured memory-recall and retrieval scores among compared systems. On MultiChallenge, MARS trails the strongest static system overall but approaches its performance at lower recorded cost on a mechanism-focused subset. Together, these results support a favorable quality-memory-cost trade-off for long-history, memory-dependent interaction.

papers.title: A $\mathrm{GL}_3$ level analog of Selberg's result for $S(t)$
papers.abstract: Let $π$ be a spherical cuspidal $\mathrm{GL}_3$ newform of prime level $N$ and trivial central character, and define $S(t,π)=π^{-1}\arg L(1/2+\textrm{i}t,π)$. Assuming the generalized Riemann hypothesis for $L(s,π)$, we establish an asymptotic formula for each fixed weighted moment of $S(t,π)$ as $N\to\infty$, for fixed $t>0$. Consequently, under the same weights, $S(t,π)/\sqrt{\log\log N}$ converges in distribution to a centered Gaussian distribution of variance $1/(2π^2)$. The key input is a weighted orthogonality formula derived from the Kuznetsov formula of prime level.

authors.name: Qingfeng Sun
authors.institution: Collaborative Innovation Center of Quantum Matter

papers.title: Causal Discovery beyond Conditional Independence: Identifiability, Algorithms, and Statistical Inference for Directed Acyclic and Cyclic Graphs
papers.abstract: Learning causal structure from data requires assumptions about mechanisms, noises, observation schemes, and interventions. Historically, causal discovery has relied primarily on conditional independence. This review focuses on modern causal discovery methods that exploit properties of distributions beyond conditional independence. Our organizing principle separates the source of identification from the statistical estimator and its computational implementation. This perspective connects conditional-independence methods with distributional asymmetries, conditional-moment restrictions, and variation across environments or individuals. We examine discovery under latent confounding and feedback, distinguishing causal information about observed variables from reconstruction of latent structure and emphasizing the additional semantics required by cyclic models. We also distinguish population identification, frequentist and Bayesian consistency, uncertainty quantification, and algorithmic guarantees. Throughout, examples show why the same observational distribution can support different conclusions under different model classes. We conclude with guidance for comparing methods at their identifiable targets and a research agenda for uncertainty, heterogeneous populations, non-scalar variables, and the intersection of discrete data, feedback, and hidden confounding.

papers.title: Solvability of complex Hessian equations corresponding to right-Noetherian polynomials
papers.abstract: On compact Hermitian manifolds, we establish a framework using radial normalization for the solvability of complex Hessian equation in form type, corresponding to right-Noetherian polynomials whose coefficients may not be constant functions. The solvability of a radial normalized equation is characterized by the existence of a C-subsolution at radial slope, which extends the results of Guo-Song to this setting.

authors.name: Junbang Liu
authors.institution: Research Institute of Petroleum Exploration and Development

papers.title: Singular vectors of sparse random rectangular matrices: Transition between delocalized and semilocalized phases
papers.abstract: Consider the bipartite Erdős--Rényi graph $\mathbb{G}(n,m,d/\sqrt{mn})$ at the critical sparsity $d = b\log(N)$ for some $b > 0$ with $N = n + m$, and constant aspect ratio $γ= n/m \geq 1$. We show that the spectrum of its centered and rescaled bi-adjacency matrix, whose limiting law is the Marčenko--Pastur (MP) distribution, is split into two phases: in the bulk, singular vectors are completely delocalized, while near the edges, singular vectors are semilocalized, with their mass concentrating on small disjoint balls, centered at vertices with extreme degrees. As $b$ decreases, we identify sharp thresholds for the emergence of outlier singular values. For explicit $b_{\rm R}^{\star}$ and $b_{\rm L}^{\star}$ as functions of $γ$, we prove that when $b > b_{\rm R}^{\star}$, there is no outlier outside the bulk; when $b_{\rm L}^{\star}< b < b_{\rm R}^{\star}$, only right outliers emerge; and when $b < b_{\rm L}^{\star}$, outliers are present on both sides, all with high probability. This removes an extra technical condition from our previous work arxiv:2508.01456, providing a complete characterization of the parameter space. In sparser regimes, in terms of left outliers, we provide some nontrivial generating mechanisms, demonstrating that local graph structure plays a key role in understanding extreme singular values. Our proofs rely on two technical inputs: (1) an entrywise local law in the MP bulk, where the deterministic equivalent of the resolvent depends on both variance profiles and normalized vertex degrees, different from the Gaussian setting; (2) spectral radius upper bounds for nonbacktracking matrices constructed from regularized random graphs, recently developed in arXiv: 2609.26615. Our results reveal fruitful phenomena for sparse random rectangular matrices at criticality, which are beyond the universality class of their Gaussian counterparts.

papers.title: Generic vanishing for Dolbeault cohomology of mixed Hodge modules on abelian varieties
papers.abstract: We study generic vanishing for the Dolbeault cohomology of mixed Hodge modules, where the differentials in the Dolbeault complex are modified by a one-form. We prove that, on the Dolbeault moduli space of Higgs line bundles, the cohomology support loci of mixed Hodge modules agree with the images of the cohomology support loci of their underlying $\mathscr{D}$-modules on the de Rham moduli space under the map induced by the nonabelian Hodge correspondence. We further apply this result to study Fourier-Mukai transforms of mixed Hodge modules on abelian varieties. We show that the extended Fourier-Mukai transform for bounded complexes of mixed Hodge modules has cohomology sheaves that are flat over the twistor line of $λ$-connections. This also gives an extension of Fourier transform of mixed Hodge modules to a compactification of the de Rham moduli space.

papers.title: ARBOR: Locating Reasoning Failures in Long Chains of Thought through Reasoning State Tracking
papers.abstract: Large reasoning models solve complex problems through long chains of thought, in which prior work has documented failure modes such as overthinking, underthinking, and unsupported deductions. Existing methods detect these failures from local signals: textual similarity to nearby steps, switch tokens, or an LLM's judgment of a step's correctness. However, what a step contributes to the solution depends on the state that earlier steps have established, so identifying failures requires a global view that tracks that state across the trajectory. Therefore, we propose ARBOR, a reasoning-failure attribution framework that represents each trajectory as a tree of reasoning states, built as each step creates, verifies, prunes, or revisits a state, and attributes each failure to a relation between a step and the state preceding it. Using ARBOR, we refine the three failure modes into distinct subtypes that harm reasoning through different mechanisms and at different costs. We find that the tree state ARBOR maintains before a step separates failure steps from the at-risk steps at which the failure did not occur. We discuss how ARBOR integrates with existing mitigations at inference time and in training data. Code, data and interactive examples are available at https://inklab.usc.edu/ARBOR.

papers.title: On the existence of mixed orthogonal arrays of strength two with six factors
papers.abstract: Orthogonal arrays are foundational objects in combinatorial design theory and experimental design theory, with broad applications in computer science, coding theory, and cryptography. In this paper, we investigate the existence for mixed orthogonal arrays of strength two with six factors, and propose several new constructions based on incomplete orthogonal Latin squares, incomplete transversal designs, and $Σ$-resolvable transversal designs. As a result, we show that the necessary conditions for the existence of such mixed orthogonal arrays are also sufficient, except for a small number of known exceptions and nine unsettled cases.

papers.title: Generalized length-gauge time-dependent Liouville equation
papers.abstract: The length-gauge (LG) time-dependent Liouville equation is a major workhorse to simulate ultrafast dynamics. The equation features the commutator between the density operator $\hatρ$ and the position operator ${\bf r}$, $\langle n{\bf k}|[{\bf r},\hatρ]|m{\bf k}'\rangle$, where $|n{\bf k}\rangle$ and $|m{\bf k}'\rangle$ are Bloch states for bands $n$ and $m$ at crystal momenta ${\bf k}$ and ${\bf k}'$, respectively. This commutator has two irreconcilable versions: Kohn and Luttinger (Phys. Rev. ${\bf 108}$, 590 (1954)) have two partial derivatives with respect to ${\bf k}$ and ${\bf k}'$, but Aversa and Sipe (AS) (Phys. Rev. B ${\bf 52}$, 14636 (1995)) have one partial derivative and one Dirac delta. For several decades, this outstanding discrepancy has received little attention. Here, we show that the generalized LG time-dependent Liouville equation has two partial derivatives, but no Dirac delta. Physically, the ${\bf k}$-off-diagonal matrix elements of the position operator provide a channel by which the electric field generates ${\bf k}$-off-diagonal matrix elements for $\hatρ$ in LG. The discrepancy emerges when the position matrix is assumed to be diagonal in ${\bf k}$. Consequently the AS' equation is a limiting case of our generalized Liouville equation, where the relative momentum ${\bf Q}$ between two states is ignored. Our numerical test reveals that the ${\bf k}$-diagonal formalism yields qualitatively different results and underestimates both energy absorption and polarization by a factor of 7. Our study establishes a general formalism for the length-gauge time-dependent Liouville equation and opens the door for future research on the ultrafast time scale, while prior results based on the ${\bf k}$-diagonal only equation may need to be revisited.

papers.title: On the Position Bias of Large Language Models: A Comprehensive Study
papers.abstract: Recent studies have shown that position bias remains a critical vulnerability in large language models (LLMs), undermining both the integrity of multiple-choice evaluations and the reliability of retrieval-augmented generation. However, existing understanding of this phenomenon is largely derived from studies with limited model coverage and English-centric benchmarks, leaving the behavior of frontier models and diverse languages underexplored. In this work, we conduct a comprehensive investigation of position bias across model scales ranging from billion-level to trillion-level parameters, covering both multiple-choice and multi-document tasks in five languages. Our experiments reveal that while position bias remains noticeable in small-scale models and Non-English languages, increasing model scale and employing standard Chain-of-Thought prompting significantly mitigate this issue. Moreover, we demonstrate that emerging \emph{thinking models} with extended reasoning capabilities are nearly immune to position bias, suggesting a costly but general approach toward resolving this vulnerability.

authors.name: Taro Watanabe
authors.institution: Nara Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: RAMP: Toward Ubiquitous Quantum-Safe Key Distribution as a Service
papers.abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) offers a security foundation independent of computational hardness assumptions. However, its reliance on specialized hardware limits access by ordinary users. Turning QKD into a service poses a fundamental trust challenge, as the providers that supply QKD-derived material themselves could retain knowledge of the keying inputs of users. This makes end-to-end confidentiality solely depend on the trustworthiness of the service infrastructure. We present RAMP, a service-oriented framework that decouples QKD material generation from key consumption. Providers operate QKD infrastructure and supply raw-key materials, while users securely acquire, mask, and locally process them into final keys without operating QKD devices. RAMP employs reconciliation-preserving masking compatible with both DV- and CV-QKD. It mitigates the trust dependence by separating the QKD-service and user-side masking domains. We formalize complementary confidentiality guarantees: RAMP protects the final key even if colluding providers expose their complete raw-key views, provided the masking domain remains secure; conversely, exposing the complete masking state does not break final-key secrecy as long as the QKD source and acquisition paths remain protected. The results establish the dual-domain security boundary of RAMP. We implement RAMP using experimentally acquired QKD data and standardized quantum-safe cryptography. After acquiring service-provisioned keying material, commodity endpoints complete user-side QKD post-processing with an average key-distillation throughput of 2.1Kb/s on an M4 Pro CPU. To our knowledge, we demonstrate the first experimental realization of such service-provisioned, user-side QKD processing, presenting a viable path toward QKD as a service.

authors.name: Sebastian Kish
authors.institution: Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation

papers.title: Coherent phonons in photoexcited semiconductors from first principles
papers.abstract: Coherent phonons are phase-locked lattice vibrations that provide a sensitive probe of nonequilibrium dynamics in materials. Existing first-principles equation-of-motion (EOM) approaches have successfully described coherent phonons in metals and semimetals, but their extension to semiconductors requires treating the long-lived electron--hole plasma created by above-gap excitation. Here we extend the first-principles EOM framework to photoexcited semiconductors by incorporating the residual plasma force that shifts the lattice equilibrium together with the plasma-induced renormalization of the electronic structure. For monolayer MoTe$_2$, the calculated carrier-density-dependent Te displacement agrees with constrained density-functional perturbation theory only when the renormalized band structure is included. We then show that increasing the photoexcited carrier density enhances both the initial total force and the plasma-shifted equilibrium position of the $A_{1g}$ mode, producing larger coherent lattice oscillations. This density-controlled response appears in both the atomic displacement and the coherent-phonon-induced band renormalization, providing complementary signatures for ultrafast reflectivity and time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.

papers.title: SenseSwarm: Swarm Exploration via Neural Structure Estimation with Shared World-Anticipation for Rapid Mapping
papers.abstract: A robot swarm covers a building faster with more robots, but the map is only as complete as the space the robots have physically visited. We target the amount of an unknown building a decentralized swarm knows at each instant, ahead of physical coverage. SenseSwarm serves a lightweight learned map predictor on the swarm's shared occupancy map and folds the predicted structure back into a stigmergic guidance field. Its 709K-parameter predictor is fine-tuned on the swarm's own multi-front observations, which we show is necessary: a single-robot predictor collapses on such views. We build a benchmark of twelve real building floors from HouseExpo, HKUST, and KTH, up to 24,000 square meters, and run 1,620 simulations across nine coordination methods, swarm sizes 32 to 512, and three seeds. On physical coverage the swarm is near parity with a greedy frontier planner, as expected. On map reconstruction, every non-predictive baseline needs 1.3 to 1.9 times longer to reach an 80 percent known map, and SenseSwarm holds an equal-time area lead of about 670 square meters, up to 1,359. Folding the prediction into the shared field matters: the same predictor applied per robot matches our speed but suffers a 6.9 times higher inter-robot contact rate at 512 robots. The prediction is computed once per shared map, so its cost stayed flat from 32 to 512 robots.

papers.title: DICL-Qwen3VL: Decoupled Confidence Calibration for Interpretable Workwear Detection
papers.abstract: Poor illumination and occlusion obscure clothing cues in indoor work sites, while diverse clothing styles complicate workwear compliance judgments. Although vision-language models (VLMs) support localization and semantic reasoning, their predictions often lack explicit supporting evidence, and a single confidence score cannot distinguish visual uncertainty from ambiguity in compliance judgments. We propose DICL-Qwen3VL, a decoupled interpretable VLM that integrates structured workwear detection, evidence generation, and separate visual and reasoning confidence estimates. First, low-rank adaptation (LoRA) adapts Qwen3-VL to localize visible upper-body clothing and identify workwear. Second, decoupled calibration separates visual observations from compliance reasoning and assigns a confidence score to each. Token entropy and sensitivity to image perturbations provide supervision for visual confidence, linking confidence estimation to the generated observations and their dependence on image content. Finally, group relative policy optimization (GRPO) jointly optimizes detection accuracy, output validity, and confidence calibration. Experiments on the company-collected Indoor Construction Site Workwear Dataset (ICSWD) and the web-collected Indoor Construction Workwear Dataset (WICWD) yield mAP@50 values of 0.730 and 0.753, respectively, outperforming the evaluated LoRA-adapted VLM baselines, including Qwen3-VL. The framework also provides explicit evidence and separate confidence scores to support manual review in industrial safety monitoring. WICWD is publicly available at https://github.com/DaErwen1/WICWD.

authors.institution: Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China

authors.name: Chao He
authors.institution: Institute of Materials Research and Engineering

papers.title: Hidden Staggered Superconducting Order in V2Se2O-Family Altermagnets
papers.abstract: $η$ pairing describes a staggered superconducting condensate whose order parameter changes sign between neighboring unit cells while maintaining a uniform magnitude. Nearly four decades after its theoretical proposal by C. N. Yang, a material platform for stabilizing $η$ pairing has remained elusive. Here, we reveal that altermagnetism, despite being pair breaking for conventional BCS pairing, naturally favors $η$-like pairing in V$_2$Se$_2$O-family altermagnets. Their valley-contrasting spin structure gives rise to oppositely spin-polarized, symmetry-related valleys centered at $X=(π,0)$ and $Y=(0,π)$, which form spin-singlet pairing partners separated by the commensurate momentum $\mathbf Q=(π,π)$, thereby favoring an $η$-like condensate. Self-consistent calculations demonstrate that the resulting $η$-like state remains robust over broad variations of chemical potential, hopping parameters, and Fermi-surface topology. To detect this hidden staggered order, we propose a phase-sensitive Josephson measurement with a uniform superconductor, where destructive interference suppresses single-Cooper-pair tunneling while preserving two-Cooper-pair processes. This constitutes a charge-$4e$-like Josephson response despite a bulk condensate composed of charge-$2e$ Cooper pairs, providing a direct phase-sensitive signature of the otherwise elusive $η$-like condensate in V$_2$Se$_2$O-family altermagnets.

authors.name: Chun Yu Wan
authors.institution: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Xiangxi Zhang
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Streamwise dispersion with interphase mass transfer through a tube
papers.abstract: Reactive solute transport in shear flows is of broad importance in chemical engineering, liquid--solid chromatography, and environmental mechanics, particularly in flow reactors and fluidic devices involving interphase mass transfer. Based on the recently developed streamwise dispersion theory for inert solutions (Guan & Chen, 2024, J. Fluid Mech., vol. 980, A33), we present an analytical model for reactive dispersion of chemically active solutes characterized by first-order, irreversible surface reactions. The extension is not a simple perturbation because the reactive boundary destroys mass conservation with streamwise and radial derivatives coupled. The model establishes how the microscopic kinetic reactivity and radial eigenmodes combine to determine a newly defined (effective) local exchange rate. We derive rigorous explicit solutions for the local moments, concentration, and phenomenological transport coefficients at arbitrary reactivity, in quantitative agreement with numerical simulations across all regimes. For tube Poiseuille flows, we reveal pre-asymptotic behaviours including sign-changing radial exchange, reactivity-enhanced drift, reactivity-reduced dispersivity, and non-Gaussian concentration profiles. Small- and large-Damköhler-number asymptotics for the local and global transport coefficients identify the reaction-limited and diffusion-limited regimes, connecting the conservative case to the Dirichlet limit at infinite reactivity. This streamwise perspective could advance our understanding of macroscale transport in chemically active systems.

authors.name: Mingyang Guan
authors.institution: Agency for Science, Technology and Research

papers.title: Sharp asymptotics for the Lovász number of random circulant graphs
papers.abstract: We study the LOVÁSZ number of dense random circulant graphs generated by independent Bernoulli bits indexed by cyclic distances. Although only $O(n)$ independent random inputs determine $O(n^2)$ globally dependent edge indicators, we prove sharp expectation asymptotics along all odd orders, including composite orders, with leading constant one. This resolves a conjecture posed for random circulant graphs in 2025. The proof combines an exact Fourier reduction and complementary duality with a positive interior smoothing that reveals a nonlinear random fixed-point equation. To analyze this equation under the strong dependence of the distance-bit model, we construct canonical tree fields, establish growing-degree Gaussian approximations through polynomial comparison and Wick/Hermite expansions, and transfer the resulting approximation back to the original sign model. A deterministic residual estimate together with an explicit exceptional-event integration yields the sharp expectation asymptotics.

authors.name: Yanqing Hu
authors.institution: Southern University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Luzhen Yang
authors.institution: University of Shanghai for Science and Technology

papers.title: Converter-Aware Coordination of Computing Flexibility in Behind-the-Meter Data Centers
papers.abstract: Data centers are emerging as large electricity consumers whose demand can be reshaped through workload scheduling. However, computing flexibility in behind-the-meter facilities does not automatically translate into electrically realizable power flexibility. Ignoring converter and network operating limits may cause converter overloads, protection trips, and interruptions to power supply and computing services. This paper proposes a converter-aware intraday scheduling methodology. First, a task-level mixed-integer linear formulation preserves synchronous training configurations and completion requirements, while Minkowski-sum aggregation and Shapley--Folkman convexification yield a linear inference-pool representation without unit-level binary variables. The latter admits a conditional relative relaxation-gap bound that decreases inversely with pool size. Second, a four-node electrical model links computing demand, on-site injections, and grid exchange to converter and network limits through lifted voltage variables and second-order cone relaxation. Finally, a mixed-integer model coordinates workloads, photovoltaic generation, energy storage, and grid purchases. Case studies show that electrical limits reshape scheduling and renewable utilization, while on-site resources reduce grid dependence. Under the studied conditions, fixed training cannot support full inference service within voltage limits, whereas coordinated scheduling achieves negligible inference shortage and passes verification against the original alternating-current model. These findings demonstrate the role of computing--electrical coordination in realizing the operational value of workload flexibility.

papers.title: DiffusionRVGE: Reinforcement Learning via Regression-Based Value Gradient Estimation
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning improves diffusion models using rewards on generated images, but repeated denoising and gradient estimation make training expensive. We introduce \method, an efficient method that constructs useful update directions by regressing centered rewards on centered final denoised images. It requires neither reward derivatives nor adjoint backpropagation through the sampling trajectory. A unified first-variation formulation identifies the value-gradient target with or without a trajectory-KL penalty. A population analysis under Gaussian noising explains the regression geometry, while a subspace analysis motivates clean-image coordinates. The implementation adapts rollout bandwidth and query weights to reward continuity: local rollouts suit smooth rewards, whereas broader groups provide informative contrasts for discrete rewards. Trained jointly on five rewards, one SD3.5-Medium model matches or exceeds DiffusionNFT's joint model on seven of eight metrics, reaching GenEval $0.94$, OCR $0.92$, and PickScore $23.82$ at about one fifth of its estimated training compute. In single-reward training, \method reaches matched reward thresholds $2.1$--$6.7\times$ faster than reproduced DiffusionNFT on identical hardware. Ablations support the clean-image estimator, direct direction transfer, and reward-dependent rollout choices. Code is available at https://github.com/jy-wang-tsinghua/DIFFUSIONRVGE.

authors.name: Jiayuan Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Hypergraphs of Low Degree Without Independent Transversals
papers.abstract: For every fixed $k\ge 3$ and every integer $b\ge 2$, we construct a finite vertex-partitioned $k$-uniform hypergraph with blocks of size $b$ and no independent transversal. We show that the maximum number of edges meeting a block is $\left(\frac{(k-1)^{k-1}}{k^k}+O_k(b^{-1})\right)b^k,$ while the maximum vertex degree is $\left(\frac{(k-2)^{k-2}}{(k-1)^{k-1}}+O_k(b^{-1})\right)b^{k-1}$. This shows that the known bound on the number of edges meeting a block is asymptotically sharp even when the leading constant in the maximum vertex degree tends to zero, which answers a problem of Groenland, Kaiser, Treffers, and Wales. By blowing up the same construction, we further obtain for arbitrarily large $n$, there exists a $k$-uniform hypergraph with $n$ blocks, each of size at least $n$, and $Δ(G)<\left(1-\frac1k\right)^{k-1}n^{k-1}$, but with no independent transversal. This gives a negative answer to a problem of Haxell and Wdowinski.

papers.title: Spectral Schwarz Lemmas and Parallel Obstructions to Metric Comparison
papers.abstract: In this paper, we characterize when comparison of contracted Chern curvatures implies comparison of Hermitian bundle metrics with the same constant on compact Hermitian bases. If the curvature contraction of the reference metric is semipositive, this implication holds for every Hermitian metric if and only if the kernel of this contraction contains no nonzero subbundle parallel with respect to the Chern connection of the reference metric. The equality terms of a $C^2$ spectral truncation identify the parallel summand on which comparison can fail, without regularity assumptions on the curvature kernel. We also establish a sharp operator estimate, with a constant independent of the bundle ranks, for holomorphic bundle maps on complete Kähler bases under curvature bounds and bounded base-map energy density. Smooth Schatten moments give global control without a separate boundedness assumption on the bundle map. Finally, we obtain rank bounds and conditions for vanishing on compact Hermitian bases from directional curvature traces over fiber subspaces. For higher-dimensional subspaces, these conditions allow mixed signs on individual fiber lines.

authors.name: Xu Pang
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

authors.name: Ren Xin-An
authors.institution: China University of Mining and Technology

papers.title: QuarkShard: Decomposing Cross-Shard Requests into Single-Input Transactions
papers.abstract: Sharding blockchains enhance scalability by distributing the workload across multiple shards. Within sharding blockchains, securely and efficiently processing cross-shard user requests remains a pivotal challenge. Traditional sharding blockchain protocols execute cross-shard requests under a processing paradigm that treats each user request as a monolithic entity to preserve its atomicity, inherently introducing significant intra-shard BFT execution overhead and cross-shard communication overhead. We propose QuarkShard, a sharding protocol that breaks away from this traditional paradigm to achieve intra-shard and cross-shard overheads below the lower bounds imposed by conventional approaches.
